articles.title: Jaxson Dart, Caleb Williams and Jayden Daniels are all hurt — here's what it means for their fantasy football weapons
articles.summary: It's been a nightmare start to 2026 for three quarterbacks who the fantasy football community has been greatly invested in.
articles.body:
What started as a promising 2026 season with a Week 1 win over the Cowboys has quickly turned into a nightmare for the Giants. Jaxson Dart, coming off an encouraging start to a big second season, left the game on Monday night following a knee injury after just seven snaps. It turns out it was worse than initially expected, and he'll now miss the rest of 2026 .

This not only makes the Giants' outlook murky for the rest of the season, but it also clouds next offseason. Has Dart shown enough in what's ultimately a limited sample to no-doubt walk into 2027 with him as the team's unquestioned starter? I'm generally Dart-positive but I'm not sure we have a clear answer on that, and I'd be shocked if a coaching staff that didn't draft him doesn't feel some uncertainty, now and in the future.

As for the rest of this season, the Giants are in big trouble. Fantasy gamers will likely remember Jameis Winston 's various scam production moments as a relief starter, most recently with the 2024 Cleveland Browns . I'm not sure if this version of Winston or the Giants offense can be one of those units. Winston looked like a player who spent all offseason as a content creator, not preparing to be a 15-game starter in the NFL. He completed zero passes of 20-plus air yards in Week 2 and had the ball die on him in the air. To be fair, he wasn't prepared to play significant snaps — not a savory note for a backup — and the Rams provide a tough defensive challenge. Yet, we should still be skeptical about Winston captaining a run-first, bully-ball offense that John Harbaugh and co. likely want to operate with in New York.

I'd feel more confident about the proceedings if Malik Nabers was 100% healthy; he's objectively not right now. Not only is Nabers clearly still working his way back from his knee injury, he also had his shoulder act up on Monday night.

The contact looked quite mild in the moment against a Rams defender but this is an issue Nabers has been dealing with dating back to his early collegiate days . It's not the first time this has flared up at the NFL level. This is merely reckless speculation on my part but you have to wonder: if the season goes south in New York with Winston at quarterback, does Nabers eventually shut it down to fix this long-term shoulder irritation, rehab from his knee injury and just return as his best self in 2027?

Nabers being compromised is a significant issue for the Giants because not only is he a near-elite player at his best, the dropoff from him to WR2 is steep. Darnell Mooney leads the team in routes run but has only been targeted on 8.8% of those patterns. I like rookie Malachi Fields but he's a blend between a dirty work power slot and downfield ball-winner, not a true high-volume option just yet.

Tight end Isaiah Likely has 18 targets through two weeks and, with the lowest air yards per target figure (6.4) among the main pass-catchers, is the most likely option to be able to survive inevitable volatility with Winston starting. I'd posit that he's still a fringe TE1 given the current landscape. Even on plays with Nabers on the field, Likely has been targeted on 33% of his routes — that jumps to 35% on plays with Winston in Week 2.

In the backfield, Cam Skattebo has become a bit less secure as a fantasy play even before the Dart injury, and I can't convince myself this helps matters. While Skattebo holds a 67% share of the running back touches, he only maintains a narrow lead on Devin Singletary (31 to 25) in routes run and has one fewer target. He also lost some touches inside the five-yard line to Najee Harris . Skattebo needs to be a true workhorse to be anything more than a boom-or-bust RB2 on a suddenly shaky offense. So far, he's not.

For the second consecutive season, Jayden Daniels has now dislocated his left elbow. The team is still weighing its options when it comes to the length of his absence but he will miss multiple weeks, at best. It's an unbelievably bad break for a team that once had all the hope in the world thanks to Daniels amid an NFC Championship Game run during his rookie season.

The good news for those invested in the offense is that Marcus Mariota is one of the league's best backup quarterbacks. Since 2024, Mariota's 7.51 adjusted yards per attempt ranks top-15 at the position, sandwiched between Justin Herbert and Dak Prescott . His 48% dropback success rate is just a tick off Jayden Daniels' 48.8%. This is a new offensive attack, in theory, under David Blough , but they still rank 29th in under-center rate and fifth in rate of plays with three or more wide receivers on the field. Washington remains in the shotgun spread world that Mariota has always functioned well within.

Mariota starting isn't the worst news in the world for the playmakers and he even has good history with Terry McLaurin . However, McLaurin has been ceding priority looks to Stefon Diggs . McLaurin has been targeted on 18.8% of his routes to 31% for Diggs. Rookie Antonio Williams has also been eating into the passing distribution, with 43% of snaps to date. He needs more reps, not fewer, based on his tape. That makes McLaurin's weekly volume difficult to trust.

McLaurin was a hair away from a monster game in Week 2 with a few narrow misses at the catch point. He may be a buy-low at some point, but with a matchup against the Seahawks, who run cover-six at a league-high rate of 36% of their defensive dropbacks, per Fantasy Points Data, it's hard to imagine McLaurin getting the vertical targets he needs.

At this point, given their usage and the way Diggs is playing in isolation, he should be the odds-on favorite to lead the team in receiving. I offered this possibility when he was signed, too. Diggs' Reception Perception charting has been quite consistent from 2024 to 2025 and he's still operating at that level in Washington. He also runs his routes underneath, in the areas where you can at least access throws against Seattle . I'd bet he gets off to a better start with Mariota under center.

Overall, while Mariota can hold down the fort for the pass-catchers' value in fantasy, the Commanders offensive line is a mess and the scheme hasn't quite gelled just yet. I doubt we'll see the absence of Daniels make any of that better over the course of the next month or so.

Of the three quarterback injuries we saw in Week 2, it sounds like Caleb Williams' will be the one that comes with the fewest amount of games missed. If I were to guess, Williams misses at least Week 3 against the Eagles on Monday night. The big hurdle is that backup Tyson Bagent also entered concussion protocol this week, so QB3 Case Keenum could be in line to start.

The last time we saw Keenum play in the regular season was when he started for the Houston Texans on Christmas Eve in 2023, averaging 3.6 yards per attempt against the Browns. I don't have to tell you that the 38-year-old veteran drawing a start against the Vic Fangio-constructed Eagles defense would not be ideal.

We already have some usage- and results-questions regarding the Bears' pass-catchers as it is. Rome Odunze returned to a full-time role after playing sparingly in Week 1, but Colston Loveland was used as a blocker to help out against Brian Flores' defense in Week 2 and Luther Burden III isn't playing enough outside of three-receiver looks.

I am still quite high on this Bears offense over the course of the season and generally believe in all three of these young players. Burden's usage is the most troubling at the present moment but for now, I'm willing to chalk that up to a training camp groin injury forcing a slow start.

In a few weeks, I'll want to buy low on the pieces of this unit. For Week 3, with a backup quarterback one way or another, I'm not sure any of these guys will be anything more than a volatile FLEX option.

articles.title: Savannah State volleyball begins SIAC play with young team (DNP)
articles.summary: Savannah State volleyball has started the season 2-10 after a loss to Edward Waters Tuesday.
articles.body:
SAVANNAH, Ga. (WSAV) — Savannah State volleyball has started the season 2-10 after a loss to Edward Waters Tuesday.

Before that the Lady Tigers went 1-3 at the first SIAC crossover. They earned a win over Central State, and fell to Kentucky State, Spring Hill College, and Miles College.

Savannah state is battling with a young team. The roster features seven freshman, five sophomores, three juniors, and only one senior.

Head coach Roselidah Obunaga said the team is learning fast, and have theirs eyes set to make the SIAC tournament at the end of the season.

"They really don't have anything to lose at this point because they're just getting started," said Obunaga.

Savannah State's next match will be against Clark Atlanta on Thursday, Sep. 24 at 6:00 p.m.

articles.title: Madl, Riggs lead Joplin in 12-8 win over Nixa
articles.summary: Joplin High School senior Jessica Madl homered and both she and junior Grace Riggs logged three hits each Tuesday to lead the Joplin Eagles to a 12-8 win ove...
articles.body:
Joplin High School senior Jessica Madl homered and both she and junior Grace Riggs logged three hits each Tuesday to lead the Joplin Eagles to a 12-8 win over the Nixa High School Eagles (5-11) at NHS.

Madl finished 3 for 3 with three runs and an RBI.

Riggs was 3 for 4 with two RBIs and one run while hitting from the nine hole.

"Jessica had a great night for us offensively," Joplin head coach Jaren Hulette said. "She got a big inning started for us with a great hit bunt, and then later in the game, she squared the ball up and came through with an important run for us. Grace Riggs was seeing the ball really well tonight and gave us a ton of production from the bottom of the lineup. She did a great job of getting on base and flipping the lineup over."

In addition to Madl and Riggs' performances at the plate, Mariah Hagans and Jasmine Diaz both went 2 for 4 with two RBIs each. Brylee Mitchell finished 1 for 4 with two RBIs and two runs.

Hagans got Joplin on the board with a line drive to center that scored Samantha Hobson in the top of the first.

Nixa's MaKiah Johnson tied the game with a solo homer in the bottom of the frame, but Joplin regained the lead in the top of the second courtesy of a Riggs' single to left that plated Madl.

Joplin increased its lead to 7-1 with five runs in the top of the fourth. Riggs drove in Madl with another single to left. Mitchell singled to left and three Joplin players — Taylor Love, Raegan Diaz and Riggs — all scored on a Nixa error. Bella Munn made it a 7-0 game when she hit a line drive double to left that scored Mitchell.

Madl swatted a solo homer over the center field fence to increase the Joplin lead to 8-1 in the top of the fifth but Nixa was able to plate a pair of runs in the bottom of the inning when Tenley Piwko drove in Bradey Harper and Johnson with a single to left.

Joplin responded with three runs in the top of the sixth to take an 11-3 lead. Hagans plated Hobson with a single to center, and Jasmine Diaz drove in Mitchell and Caldwell with a single to right field.

Nixa trimmed the Joplin lead to 11-5 in the bottom of the inning when Harper slammed a two-run homer to center that plated Berklie Harvey.

Joplin got one of those runs back in the top of the seventh when Raegan Diaz scored on a Nixa error. In the bottom of the inning, Nixa's Johnson drew a bases-loaded walk that scored a run, Harvey scored on a Jordan Phillips' single and Ossie Cooper drove in Peyton Clopton with a single to center, but the Nixa rally fell short as Joplin held on for the 12-8 win.

"I thought it was a great team win tonight," Hulette said. "I was really proud of our approaches at the plate. We did a great job of putting pressure on Nixa's defense all seven innings."

Joplin (11-10) travels to Webb City High School (12-8-1) for a 5 p.m. game Thursday.
authors: Laurie Sisk, The Joplin Globe, Mo.

articles.title: New York Yankees vs. Tampa Bay Rays: Gerrit Cole vs. Mason Englert
articles.summary: A new-look Yankees lineup aims for a spark against the Rays as Gerrit Cole gets his last start of the regular season.
articles.body:
This late in the season and with no team goal to strive for other than to gain positive momentum heading into the postseason, it's about the little things for these two division rivals. For this particular Wednesday matchup, the biggest little thing is to follow Gerrit Cole 's work on the mound — especially in how he handles what has become a bit of a home run problem as of late, allowing a whopping eight long balls in his previous three starts.

While it is true that the Rays aren't what one might describe as a homer-happy team, particularly on the road, it's not as if Cole's recent opponents sat anywhere near the top of the HR leaderboards. We've come a long way since Cole's regular-season debut against the Rays, in which he deployed an approach we've seldom seen from him since. In that game, Cole relied on a sinker as his second most used pitch to complete six scoreless innings in the Bronx against Tampa.

It's the third different lineup for the Yankees in as many games in this series, and while that in and of itself isn't particularly newsworthy, one specific change will jump out. For the first time since his call-up, the Yankees will hit George Lombard Jr. in the second spot in the order — it comes as a reward for Lombard, who has hit safely in seven of his last eight starts.

A while ago we discussed here that even though it wasn't the ideal scenario, the Yankees might easily find themselves needing to move Lombard up in the order to balance a lineup without Judge. Judge came back and got hurt again, and the Yankees are now trying out this alternative against the right-hander Mason Englert . Much like his opponent on the mound tonight, Englert has also dealt with home run woes in recent starts, allowing five in his last two.

articles.title: All-Pro Rams WR Puka Nacua to be limited in practice again this week with hip/groin injury
articles.summary: All-Pro receiver Puka Nacua will be limited in practice again this week for the Los Angeles Rams while he recovers from an injury to his hip and groin.  Nacu...
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — All-Pro receiver Puka Nacua will be limited in practice again this week for the Los Angeles Rams while he recovers from an injury to his hip and groin.

Nacua missed the Rams' 28-6 victory over the New York Giants on Monday night, and he was held out of the Rams' walkthrough practice Wednesday.

After missing much of training camp and the preseason practice schedule with a core muscle injury, Nacua was able to play in the Rams' season-opening loss in Australia . But he missed more practice time last week after developing this latest injury, which coach Sean McVay compared to "pre-hernia" pain — while careful to specify that Nacua does not have a hernia.

"These soft-tissue issue things, I wish I had better information," McVay said. "It would be helpful for me to have a little bit more clarity as well. I want him to feel good. I know he's chomping at the bit to get out there, but he wouldn't practice (Wednesday) if we were able to go, and then (Thursday), we'll see what that looks like."

McVay said it's "more likely than not" that Nacua will practice this week, but he doesn't know whether the 2025 NFL receptions leader will play against the Denver Broncos on Sunday night. The Rams don't believe the injury has any potential to be a long-term setback.

"When you're a skill player and you're really trying to hit high-speed yards and really open up, and you feel (discomfort), it's some of the things that can almost be like pre-hernia, is kind of what he's feeling," McVay said. "So you err on the side of caution. Usually time is the best thing that allows that thing to heal, and then once you get to a certain point, I think you feel pretty good moving forward. ... I just know that he's frustrated, and we all want him to be out there, but we want him to return to performance, not just be able to just kind of gut through it."

Nacua has missed only seven games due to injury in his four-year NFL career, but he plays a physical, high-contact style of football as both a ball-carrier and a blocker. He missed five games in the 2024 season with a sprained knee, and he was slightly slowed by injuries to his chest and ankle last season.

The Rams have an abnormal number of early season injury problems for a team that has frequently avoided major long-term personnel losses during McVay's career.

Ronnie Rivers , a backup running back and key special teams player, went on injured reserve Wednesday with a calf injury. He joins All-Pro defensive end Myles Garrett , who will be out for at least three more games after undergoing knee surgery following his zero-tackle debut with his new team in Melbourne.

Safety Kam Kinchens (hamstring), receiver Jordan Whittington (quadriceps) and tight end Colby Parkinson (knee) also were unavailable for practice Wednesday.

Left tackle Alaric Jackson was limited after injuring his knee against the Giants, although he didn't miss a snap due to the minor pain. Jackson's health is particularly important for the Rams because backup David Quessenberry has barely played on offense for his past two seasons.

The Rams signed safety Maximus Pulley off the Philadelphia Eagles ' practice squad to take Rivers' spot on the 53-man roster.

articles.title: Bears' Ben Johnson tries to calm fears with post-Caleb Williams injury comments
articles.summary: Caleb Williams being out for the team's game against the Eagles isn't ideal, but Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson is saying the right things.
articles.body:
It was certainly a scary sight to see Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams go down during the team's Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings . The injury looked super rough at the time, and while it couldn't have been comfortable, at least it's just a hamstring injury, so Williams is expected to be back with the team before too long.

But Williams is still expected to miss a few games, and he's not expected to play against the Philadelphia Eagles on "Monday Night Football." Backup quarterback Tyson Bagent is also out in concussion protocol and questionable for the Week 3 matchup.

So, that leaves them with their third-stringer, the 38-year-old Case Keenum . Should Bears fans be freaking out? Not at all.

Ben Johnson has high praise for Case Keenum

Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, head coach Ben Johnson said the kind of stuff that could calm the fears of Bears fans watching. He spoke highly of Keenum.

"He's been a baller from, I think, the day that he was born, from what I can tell," Johnson told reporters, per Fox 32 Chicago . "His teammates gravitate to him. I think that's a good starting point for a quarterback."

He also talked about his age, adding, "Of course, he's up there in years a little bit, but that experience has really paid off for him. He sees the game the same way that we do. I think he accelerates through his progressions because he's seen so many things over the course of his time. He's been in so many different offenses."

Finally, Johnson said that the veteran quarterback "might be a step slower than he was when he first entered the league, and yet his mind's going so fast, it helps catch him on up. He's playing as good a football as he probably has his whole career."

So, Bears fans can feel a touch better about this strange situation. It's not unusual for a first- and second-string quarterback to be out at once, but Johnson says they're in good hands.

articles.title: What I’m hearing at Gillette Stadium: Wednesday buzz (Week 3)
articles.summary: Preparation for the Week 3 matchup between the Patriots and Jaguars is underway. Here's what we're hearing at Patriots Wire.
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass — The New England Patriots got their first win of the season, but now they are looking ahead and preparing to face off against the Jacksonville Jaguars .

"The focus has got to be on Jacksonville, and our performance," Vrabel said on Wednesday.

Mike Vrabel provides crucial injury updates

A few players left Sunday's game early due to injury, and head coach Mike Vrabel provided some crucial updates.

"I do not think Dre'Mont [Jones] will do much today, I know that he is working hard to try to get back, and we will see where he is later on in the week," he said. "And I would say that that would be the same for [Craig] Woodson.

"Q [Quintayvious Hutchins] probably won't do much today, and I think Dell [Pettus] went on IR this morning."

Cornerback Carlton Davis , who missed all of practice last week, as well as Sunday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers , was back out there on Wednesday, which is a positive sign that he will return for the matchup against Jacksonville.

However, the list of absent players was quite long, with S Craig Woodson (shoulder), OLB Dre'Mont Jones (shoulder), S Dell Pettus (IR - ankle), FB Reggie Gilliam , OLB Quintayvious Hutchins, OT Morgan Moses , and TE Eli Raridon (thigh) not being spotted during the media-attended portion.

Safety and special teams ace Brenden Schooler was also back out on the field despite having begun the season on NFI. This is a new rule that allows players on either NFI or PUP to begin practicing after Week 2, but they cannot be activated until Week 5, missing a total of four games.

Drake Maye provides analysis on where the offense stands

The Patriots' offense is off to a bit of a slower start this season, but Drake Maye remains confident, knowing they will be just fine.

"Yeah, I think we're finding ourselves. I think every time you get into a new season with new guys, new players and you're battling injuries, every team in the league is trying to improve," he explained. "Really for us, it's about finding ourselves. It's like I said at this time last year, we were kind of – I remember we were 1-2 and going into the Panthers , and we were trying to figure ourselves out. Just things like finding a rhythm on offense, getting down in the run game, doing little things and really just finding ourselves and finding a rhythm. So, I'm happy with the guys, how we practice and how we are trying to approach practice. It's really changing that and realizing how much that can translate to the games.

"So, finding ourselves, but at the same time, we have plays that are there and realizing that execution and extra effort is what we talk about in the offensive room, really making them go. Realizing that coaches can call the plays, but we've got to make them go, and realizing that you only get so many chances in the game. You only get to hit them once. So, realizing that and taking advantage of them."

The Patriots have a tall task ahead of them as the Jaguars are a team that is strong in every single area. And Vrabel highlighted a few of those, beginning with the defense.

"The size, play-making ability. Again, they created 31 turnovers, so it's tough to run the football against them," he said. "I think that they play with great technique across the front. Linebackers are active; secondaries are really good tacklers. But obviously, they want to create X plays or tackles for loss, negative plays with the guys on the edge who attack with great size, skill, power, ability to pass rush and all those different things.

He specifically referenced their defense line, calling it a "very good front."

"Yeah, I think they fly around. I think the biggest thing, they're running the football. They have a good front," the quarterback said. "Then, I think they're well-coached. You can tell they have an ability to fly to the football, try to punch it out. I think one of the best things about their defense is they can do a lot of different things in different ways. They have some guys that can attack on the edge, but also some plug-in guys that really fit their defense."

Then, there's their star quarterback, Trevor Lawrence .

"I think he is just much more decisive and comfortable," the Patriots head coach said about Lawrence's growth. "I think you could always count on some turnovers, maybe three or four years ago. I don't think that is necessarily the case now. He has done a really fantastic job of being able to move the ball downfield, but keep it out of harm's way. He's decisive when he scrambles. It's a guaranteed first down, if not longer when he decides to scramble. Those aren't even the designed run plays. Those are drop back passes that turn into play extensions, and he is either keeping his eyes downfield and hitting somebody, or he's decisive and he is willing to scramble.

"So, I just see a lot of maturity, and he is playing at a high level."

Maye also had high praise for Lawrence, talking about his past interactions with the quarterback.

"Yeah, back when I was getting recruited by Clemson early on – he grew up in Georgia and not too far from North Carolina," he said. "So, I was at camp and got to meet Trevor when he was playing and when I went on a visit. He was playing great football at Clemson, and I crossed paths with him a little bit. So, I'm a big fan of his game. I like the way he keeps on getting better year after year. You can see in the offense, especially with Coach [Liam] Coen, of him just growing and making plays. He can make a lot of different plays.

"He's mobile, can throw on the run and throw in the pocket. I remember he threw a post my first time I played him in my rookie year; that was a great throw. So, we played him one time before, and it was cool to watch. I'm looking forward to playing a guy that, he was in college when I was in high school that I looked up to, and I really enjoyed watching him play."

With Pettus being placed on injured reserve, the Patriots are planning to sign outside linebacker Jose Ramirez to the 53-man roster to take his spot.

"I'm excited to play with the guys in my room, play with this team, and just show that I can play football," Ramirez told Patriots Wire. "God blessed me with the talent to play football and I made it this far in this journey."

"I feel like I bring my work ethic. Just everything that comes with being a Patriot," he added. "Growing up, watching the Patriots, Tom Brady , Mike Vrabel, like everybody, it's just the Patriots Way. So I feel like I fit in that sense."

Ramirez, who was selected by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the 2023 NFL Draft, spent his rookie year on the practice squad before earning a spot on the 53-man roster for the 2024 season, in which he played in four games on defense and on special teams. After that, he went on to have a short stint in the Canadian Football League before signing with the Philadelphia Eagles on a futures contract on Jan. 15, 2026, but was released on Aug. 30, 2026.

"Well, he has been a really good practice player for us," Vrabel said. "I think he has improved since the time he has been here. Multiple times being recognized by taking the reps that we talk about being on the show team and using those to his advantage. So, there will be an opportunity, we'll see, for him to be able to help us this week when we get down to the 48-man roster."

The Jacksonville Jaguars have a lot of talented wide receivers, including Parker Washington , Brian Thomas Jr. , and Jakobi Meyers , as well as receiver and cornerback Travis Hunter . So, that means Christian Gonzalez might not be able to just shadow one guy, as he did against DK Metcalf last weekend.

On Wednesday, he highlighted why that receiver core is so dangerous.

"Just getting in on your film. I mean, we all know in the back end that whoever's in front of us, they're a top target on that offense," cornerback Christian Gonzalez said. "They spread the ball around, and as DBs, as corners, we love it. Me, Marcus, and CD, we invite it, and we love it being able to know they throw the ball to everybody and move the ball around. So we're excited for it and just ready to get out there."

The Patriots' run game showed some improvement in their 20-3 win, with Henderson leading the way with 76 yards on 16 carries and a touchdown, followed by Rhamondre Stevenson with six carries for 43 yards. Stevenson also finished with a fumble, which came in the passing game.

"Well, I hope that they both can help us. I think that we can all see that when we were playing well offensively, they both had major roles," Vrabel said. "It was good to see Rhamondre come back in there and have a couple really nice runs and break through a couple times. So, I think we're going to need everybody, and we know how critical the ball is and ball security, and we're going to need everybody. We're going to need his playmaking ability, and we're going to need what TreVeyon brings to the table as well."

articles.title: Cubs' Bregman on the mend after getting struck in the face by a foul ball
articles.summary: Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman is thankful he’s not a little shorter.  Sporting a discolored left eye after being struck by a foul ball in the on-de...
articles.body:
CHICAGO (AP) — Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman is thankful he's not a little shorter.

Sporting a discolored left eye after being struck by a foul ball in the on-deck circle Sunday, the three-time All-Star said it could've been worse.

"Super lucky it hit where it hit and just a lot of gratitude that it wasn't a few centimeters higher," he said before Wednesday night's game against Miami .

The ball, off the bat of teammate Michael Busch n Cincinnati , caused several facial fractures.

With the postseason approaching, the Cubs are glad the injury won't require a stint on the injured list.

Bregman said he'll likely start shagging ground balls in a day or so and will be trying out new styles of helmets to protect the eye.

"The whole left side of my face has been a little bit numb," he said.

The Cubs can clinch an NL wild-card berth with a win Wednesday night or an Arizona loss.

"He's still got significant swelling in his face and his eye that needs to improve," Chicago manager Craig Counsell said Tuesday. "But all things considered, he's in a good place."

Bregman was on deck in the fourth inning of a 9-1 win at Cincinnati when he was hit on the left side of his face by Busch's check-swing foul. Bregman immediately jogged toward the Cubs' dugout and covered his face before going back to the clubhouse with an athletic trainer.

"When everything was going down on Sunday afternoon, I think that we all thought the worst case might be a possibility," president of baseball operations Jed Hoyer said Tuesday. "And all the news since then has been really good. He's had a lot of different doctor's appointments, and they've been positive. And I think we have to take it one step at a time."

Bregman is batting .262 with 26 homers and 89 RBIs in 153 games during his first season with Chicago. He signed a $175 million, five-year contract with the Cubs in free agency.

The 32-year-old Bregman got off to a rough start in his new home, hitting just .229 with two homers in his first 20 games. But he has been one of Chicago's most productive players since the All-Star break, batting .305 with 17 homers and 48 RBIs in his last 57 games.

Bregman also has excelled in the postseason in the past. He won two World Series championships with the Houston Astros . He appeared in at least two postseason games in each of the previous nine years.

articles.title: Dodgers Lineup vs. Padres: Shohei Ohtani Returns, Not in Leadoff Spot
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers are gearing up for the second game of a three-game homestand against the San Diego Padres.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are gearing up for the second game of a three-game homestand against the San Diego Padres .

1. Mookie Betts , SS 2. Shohei Ohtani , DH 3. Will Smith , C 4. Freddie Freeman , 1B 5. Teoscar Hernandez , LF 6. Kyle Tucker , RF 7. Andy Pages , CF 8. Max Muncy , 3B 9. Tommy Edman , 2B

The Dodgers are facing a lefty in Robbie Ray , so they're leaning on their lineup with righties at the top.

With Ohtani just coming back from the injured list and Mookie Betts the hottest hitter on the team, Dave Roberts chose to play the matchup and not have Ohtani lead off.

Roberts has said Ohtani may not lead off against lefties, and true to his word, the Dodgers skipper pulled the trigger.

articles.title: Panthers place RB Jonathon Brooks on injured reserve
articles.summary: The Carolina Panthers placed backup running back Jonathon Brooks on injured reserve with a groin injury on Wednesday.
articles.body:
The Carolina Panthers placed backup running back Jonathon Brooks on injured reserve with a groin injury on Wednesday.

According to a person familiar with the situation, Brooks will have surgery Wednesday to repair a core muscle injury that will result in him missing at least six weeks. Brooks is expected to return this season, the person told The Associated Press on condition of anonymity because the team has yet to provide any details on how long he will be out.

The Panthers signed safety Isaiah Simmons from the practice squad to take Brooks' spot on the 53-man roster.

Coach Dave Canales said Monday that Brooks had injured his groin late in Carolina's 34-3 win over the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. He said at the time the team was awaiting the results of an MRI.

Brooks has struggled with knee injuries in the past, limiting his playing time to only five of a potential 36 games since joining the league as a second round pick in 2024.

He tore his ACL during his final season at Texas and then again during his rookie season with the Panthers. The injury forced him to miss the remainder of the 2024 season and all of 2025.

Brooks was used sparingly in Carolina's first two games of the season.

Chuba Hubbard is Carolina's starting running back and A.J. Dillon is third on the depth chart.

Among the veteran free agents available to sign with Carolina at running back include Austin Ekeler, who last played with the Washington Commanders in 2025, and Kareem Hunt, who played for the Kansas City Chiefs.

The Panthers play at Cleveland on Sunday.

articles.title: Somkiat Chantra To Replace Mir For Japanese Grand Prix
articles.summary: Photos by Honda. Honda has called up Somkiat Chantra to fill Joan Mir's factory seat at the Japanese Grand Prix, pulling the Thai rider off its World Superbi...
articles.body:
Honda has called up Somkiat Chantra to fill Joan Mir's factory seat at the Japanese Grand Prix, pulling the Thai rider off its World Superbike program for a one-off return to MotoGP at Motegi. HRC confirmed Chantra will ride the Honda HRC Castrol RC213V while the 2020 world champion continues a recovery and observation period .

Mir has been ruled out of rounds 16 and 17, the Japanese and Indonesian Grands Prix, on the medical advice of Dr. Angel Charte and the medical staff treating him at Barcelona's Dexeus University Hospital. His problems trace back to the San Marino GP at Misano, where he retired after five laps citing headaches and an unexplained energy shortage.

Blood work carried out while he sat out the Austrian round returned what Honda called "altered parameters," and those results remain inconclusive. Charte has ordered 15 days of strict rest. Any further news on Mir's status won't come until after the Indonesian round.

HRC test rider Takaaki Nakagami covered for Mir at the Red Bull Ring, where he impressed with 13th on his first race of the season, ahead of full-time Honda men Luca Marini and Diogo Moreira. For Motegi, however, Nakagami was already committed to a wildcard spot on a fifth RCV at his home event. This season will be the final year such premier-class wildcards are allowed, with the format outlawed from 2027, leaving Motegi one of the last opportunities to gather development data. Fellow test rider Aleix Espargaro is still working back to fitness after his Sepang back injuries.

While Chantra may not have been an obvious choice, he has a history of success at Motegi, the circuit where he took his 2023 Moto2 win and later placed 15th in last season's MotoGP round with LCR. His premier-class rookie year underwhelmed, netting seven points and 26th in the standings before he moved to Honda's WorldSBK effort for 2026.

That campaign has been derailed too, with a pre-season crash requiring surgery and delaying his adaptation to the CBR1000RR-R. He sits 20th on 10 points, having scored on seven occasions with a best of 13th.

Chantra is only confirmed for Motegi, as Indonesia's Mandalika round clashes with the WSBK's October 9-11 stop at Estoril. Honda will need another replacement for that weekend.

articles.title: Unplayed Mongolia fixture denies India shot at historic Asian Games esports medal
articles.summary: New Delhi: India’s hopes of securing a historic esports medal at the Asian Games in Japan suffered a setback after an unplayed eFootball fixture against
articles.body: New Delhi: India’s hopes of securing a historic esports medal at the Asian Games in Japan suffered a setback after an unplayed eFootball fixture against Mongolia was recorded as a forfeit win, leaving India without the goal difference it needed to remain in contention for the knockout stage.India’s eFootball pair of Chinmay Sahoo and Danial Patel, coached by Saksham Rattan, had earlier drawn 0-0 against Uzbekistan’s Abubakir Iminjonov and Farrukh Mirkhamitov. With India needing a win in its next Group F fixture, Mongolia’s Munkh-Ochir Batmanlai and Khantamir Munkh-Orgil failed to report to the Call Room within the stipulated time. India was subsequently awarded a 0-0 forfeit victory.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule | Medal TallyHowever, Uzbekistan defeated Mongolia 2-0 across the console and mobile matches and finished top of Group F. With only the group winner advancing directly to the quarterfinals, India’s campaign ended despite its awarded victory.The Esports Federation of India (ESFI) has raised concerns over the circumstances surrounding the fixture and the subsequent qualification calculations. The federation said India was denied the opportunity to actually play Mongolia, score goals and improve its goal difference, which it says was relevant to determining qualification among the teams.According to ESFI, Uzbekistan was able to play its fixture against Mongolia and subsequently benefited from the resulting goal difference before eventually winning the bronze medal. ESFI has questioned whether recording no goal difference for India’s forfeited match created an unequal sporting opportunity.The federation also cited a series of technical and scheduling disruptions. Matches scheduled for 9am reportedly began only after 11.30am due to problems with an organiser-provided playing device. The Uzbekistan-Mongolia fixture, scheduled for around 3pm, reportedly started at approximately 5pm Japan time, affecting the timing of the India-Mongolia encounter.ESFI further alleged that Mongolia had not been adequately briefed about the required Call Room reporting time and that its team manager was unable to leave the preceding match to complete the reporting process for the next fixture.The federation said India’s subsequent request for a review by the Olympic Council of Asia, the Esports Organising Committee and competition management went unacknowledged. ESFI also alleged that India was not given adequate clarity on the applicable rules within the stipulated 15-minute window to lodge a formal protest.India sought clarification on the regulatory basis for recording no goal difference in forfeited matches, the use of average points and average goal difference for ranking, the complete qualification calculations and when the ranking methodology was formally communicated to participating teams.ESFI has called for a transparent review, a written response and appropriate corrective action, while reaffirming its respect for competition rules and technical officials.India’s 15-member esports contingent is competing across four disciplines: eFootball, Puyo Puyo Champions, Pokémon UNITE and League of Legends.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: From missing Hangzhou to silver in Nagoya: Mirabai Chanu’s Asian Games redemption
articles.summary: Nagoya: Two hundred and sixty-four grams. That was all it took to complete Mirabai Chanu’s collection of heavyweight medals.
articles.body: Nagoya: Two hundred and sixty-four grams.That was all it took to complete Mirabai Chanu’s collection of heavyweight medals.The silver medallion awarded at Aichi-Nagoya weighs 264gm, but for Mirabai it could well be worth its weight in gold.Six years ago, it was also in Japan that Mirabai won an Olympic silver at the Tokyo Games. In the land of the rising sun, she delivered again, this time in a statement of persistence and resilience.At the Nagoya City Trade and Industry Centre here on Wednesday, the 32-year-old ended India’s 28-year wait for an Asian Games weightlifting medal, winning silver and, in the process, finally adding a continental medal to her cabinet.“I feel very good. This Asian Games medal was my dream and finally I got a silver medal. Since I stepped into the elite level, this has been my dream,” gushed Mirabai after her medal-winning performance.Competing in the 49kg category, the lifter, who wore tricolour hair ties, totalled 198kg (87kg in snatch + 111kg in clean and jerk) to finish behind defending champion Ri Song-gum. The North Korean was in another stratosphere altogether, lifting a world-record 215kg (94+121), a full 17kg more than the Indian. Indonesia’s Luluk Diana Tri Wijayana took bronze with 191kg (88+103).Mirabai was assured in the snatch, clearing 83kg, 85kg and 87kg without much fuss. She trailed Ri and Luluk going into the clean and jerk, but successfully negotiated 107kg and 111kg to secure silver.Asked why the continental medal was her dream and not the Olympic silverware which she already possessed, Mirabai said, “Competition in Asian weightlifting is very strong with Korea, China etc. I believe that medals in Asian Games are equal to the ones won at the Olympics. In fact, I feel the competition at the Asian Games is tougher than the Olympics.”For an athlete who had dreamed of an Asian Games podium for years, the medal was also a measure of redemption.Mirabai missed the 2018 edition because of a back injury. In Hangzhou three years ago, a hip and thigh injury hampered her during her final attempt and left her fourth.Earlier this year, a lingering shoulder injury had cast another shadow over her season. But Mirabai put that behind her by winning gold at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games.Her resilience has deep roots.Born in Nongpok Kakching in southeastern Manipur, Mirabai grew up in a landscape that is picturesque and also steeped in history and identity. The region, known for landmarks such as Kakching Garden and the People’s Museum, has also witnessed the imprint of World War II, with Langol Peak serving as a campsite for Allied forces. From that landscape emerged an athlete who has repeatedly had to rise after setbacks.If age and injuries threatened to slow her down, Mirabai had a support system that refused to let that happen. While coach Vijay Sharma took care of her training, American strength and conditioning coach Dr Aaron Horschig monitored her fitness and recovery. A nutritionist, meanwhile, ensured she stayed on top of her weight.The work that went into the medal, she said, was immense.“A lot of work. After the Commonwealth Games, there was very little time. At the same time, I had to control my weight at 48kg (for the CWG). It was very difficult for me to control my weight,” explained the Padma Shri awardee.One of the most keenly watched Indian athletes at the Games, Mirabai also had to contend with the weight of expectation.“There is pressure, but I also have confidence. The whole world has had hopes of me winning a medal. I draw strength from the fact that people think positively about me and pray for me so much. That said, the pressure of not delivering is also there,” she said.With the Asian Games medal finally ticked off her bucket list, attention inevitably turns to another question: is a fourth Olympic appearance at the 2028 Los Angeles Games on the horizon?“We haven’t finalised anything yet. But we will try. Qualifying starts in Dec. But for now, I will enjoy it,” she signed off.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Chess Olympiad Round 7: India's chances of gold get bleaker despite win in open; women still in hunt
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India will look back at Nihal Sarin's loss before the rest day and wonder what might have happened had he taken a few more minutes — he had
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India will look back at Nihal Sarin's loss before the rest day and wonder what might have happened had he taken a few more minutes — he had plenty of time on the clock, more than enough to have avoided the queen blunder that cost India their Round 6 match against Uzbekistan on Monday. When the players returned to the board for Round 7 in Samarkand on Wednesday, following Tuesday's rest day, the overall picture in the race for gold remained largely unchanged.Another hope of an Uzbek slip-up, this time at the hands of an in-form Chinese team, evaporated as the hosts won 3-1, moving a step closer to another coveted Chess Olympiad title. India's open team also won on the day, though not as comfortably as the Uzbeks.India's opponents were England, and with Dommaraju Gukesh and Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa having already wrapped up wins on their boards, the team's fate no longer rested on Nihal, which was just as well, because he lost again on Board 3, this time in a marathon 88-move battle against Luke McShane.McShane, playing white, produced a stubborn, fighting performance against the higher-rated Nihal.The Englishman took the initiative early, pushing pawns on both the queenside and kingside, while Nihal hit back with active piece play and a dangerous-looking attack on White's king.The position stayed unresolved for a long time, and by the time both players were down to their final seconds on the clock, the game had turned into a test of nerve as much as calculation.McShane held firm, found the right defensive moves under pressure, and gradually turned his rooks into the more active pieces on the board.The turning point came with 66.Re8, forcing off a pair of rooks and steering the game into a simplified endgame. This was exactly the kind of position where McShane's advanced f-pawn and increasingly active king took over.From there, he picked off Nihal's pawns one by one, and after nearly seven hours of play,Nihal resigned on move 88.It left Nihal with back-to-back individual losses at a tournament where he had otherwise been one of India's most reliable performers.India closed out the England match 2.5-1.5, with wins from Praggnanandhaa and Gukesh outweighing Nihal's loss and Arjun Erigaisi's draw.It keeps India firmly in the group chasing Uzbekistan, who remain the only team with a perfect record after seven rounds, a gap that will be hard to close with just four rounds left.Savitha Shri, a potent force for India at 2026 Chess OlympiadIf the open section's gold hopes are fading, India's women's team gave every reason to believe theirs are still very much alive, and 19-year-old Savitha Shri has been a big part of why.The Chennai-born player has now played six games at this Olympiad and won every single one, and Wednesday's win over Germany's Lara Schulze followed the same pattern.After a fairly balanced opening, Savitha. with the Whites, gradually seized control with active piece play and mounting pressure on the kingside.The position turned complicated around the 34th move, when she allowed a trade of pieces that led into a tricky rook-and-knight endgame, one she navigated calmly even as Schulze fell into serious time trouble.Savitha's rook grew increasingly active from there, picking off pawns and creating threats on both sides of the board, and though Schulze tried to fight back, Savitha never let her king come under real danger.In a phase that tested patience above all else, with both players short on time, Savitha pushed her kingside pawns forward until 88.g6+ proved decisive, leaving Schulze unable to save her rook.It capped a near-90-move grind with a well-earned win and helped India rout Germany 3.5-0.5, with Koneru Humpy and Divya Deshmukh also winning their games and Vaishali Rameshbabu drawing on Board 2.ALSO READ: Juggling Chess Olympiad prep and a commentary gig in India: The other side of USA's only female GM Irina articles.summary: The Texans got an unfortunate on veteran and starting right guard Ed Ingram ahead of their Week 3 game against the Colts. The post Texans Receive Ominous Ins...
articles.body:
The Houston Texans got unfortunate news on right guard Ed Ingram .

It came right along with the news that starting wide receiver Nico Collins is not expected to play in Week 3 against the Indianapolis Colts . Unfortunately for the Texans, Ingram is also expected to miss that game, per KPRC 2's Aaron Wilson.

Ingram is already off to an ominous start. He missed the first practice of the week on Wednesday due to the groin injury that sidelined him in Week 2 against the Cincinnati Bengals .

Ingram has been relatively durable in his career.

Texans RG Ed Ingram Not Expected to Play vs Colts

Ingram has started 56 of 63 games played in the NFL . He has never logged fewer than 14 appearances in a single season entering the 2026 campaign. He did that with the Texans in 2025. Ingram has also made at least that many starts in three of his four NFL seasons.

A former second-round pick (59th overall) of the Minnesota Vikings in 2022, his is Year 2 in Houston. His return on a three-year, $37.5 million contract was polarizing.

ESPN's Bill Barnwell called it the Texans' "worst" of the offseason.

"Among the various moves [Nick] Caserio made up front a year ago, trading a sixth-round pick to the Vikings for Ingram might have been his biggest success. Ingram had been a liability in Minnesota and was benched midway through the 2024 season," Barnwell wrote in an article published in May.

"There's a price for which bringing Ingram back would have made sense. But on this deal, Ingram is earning $15 million in 2026 and getting $5 million of the $9.25 million he's owed in 2027 guaranteed at signing."

Barwell's concern was about Ingram's pass protection remaining poor. But also the 6-foot-3, 307-pund RG's ability to maintain his run blocking prowess after a veritable breakout last season.

Ingram remained solid in the run game in Week 1. However, his pass blocking remained an issue .

articles.title: How Matt Chernoff Evolves From One Legendary Chapter to the Next at 680 the Fan
articles.summary: "I’ve always taken pride in the fact that I can work with different people. I don’t want this show to sound like Chuck & Chernoff because that chapter is clo...
articles.body:
Twenty-five years is a long time for any sports radio personality to command the airwaves in a single market. When it happens with a duo, it defines a legacy. Earlier this summer, 680 The Fan announced that changes were coming to afternoon drive and the Chuck & Chernoff show. After twenty-five years together, including the last eighteen on The Fan, Matt Chernoff and Chuck Oliver would be ending their radio program together.

"To do it in my hometown is what meant the most to me," said Chernoff about closing the chapter on Chuck & Chernoff . "Chuck and I both being born here, that's what separated us from everyone else. We spoke the language of everyone listening. The run is important, but to do it in your hometown makes it extra special."

Chuck & Chernoff first worked together in the early 2000s at AM 790 The Zone before moving to 680 The Fan in 2008. It was there that Chuck and Chernoff established themselves as a top sports talk show in Atlanta in the afternoon drive timeslot, where they resided for much of their tenure.

However, a week after signing multi-year extensions to remain with the radio station, change was in the air. Chuck Oliver announced he would depart the program but continue to host his evening program on the radio station. The response from loyal listeners was immediate.

"It was a little overwhelming to realize that at one point our show touched them at some point over the years. That was the coolest thing ever," explained Chernoff. "It wasn't adding up in my head. Because when you're doing the show, it's like any other line of work. Then the years just add up. Then you get to the end, and you realize the generations that just wanted to hang out. That's the greatest compliment ever."

Chernoff says the chemistry clicked early between himself and Oliver. They quickly learned each other's tells, delivery and personalities. Chernoff said he never felt like he had to fight for microphone time, instead comparing their execution to a dance.

A month after Oliver's announcement, the program bid its final farewell. The show featured some of Atlanta's top sports icons and frequent guests, keeping the focus on honoring the program's legacy while also enjoying a laugh along the way.

"We have a line. Our show was football and funny. Football ninety percent of the time, and hopefully the other ten percent was funny and gave people a laugh," said Chernoff. "We're lucky we had a chance to close up shop like we did. That doesn't happen too often in this business. I'm so proud of the show. It wasn't perfect, but it was something you could step back and see how rare it was."

At the end of August, Chernoff welcomed a new voice to afternoons on The Fan, but an all-too-familiar face to the radio station. John Kincade rejoined the station six years after departing for an opportunity in mornings at 97.5 The Fanatic in his hometown of Philadelphia. The pairing was "super comfortable" for Chernoff as he entered his second act in afternoon drive.

"John and I have known each other for a million years. When we knew that was going to be the decision, John and I jumped on the phone. He's so easy to work with," said Chernoff. "As soon as it was presented to me, I knew this would be great. He's never shy with an opinion and as pro as it gets."

Chernoff didn't have any reservations about the decision, which he admitted was stunning to some when the news became public in early August. However, he now had a co-host who could focus solely on growing the afternoon program instead of attempting to balance two shows, as Oliver had successfully done for so many years.

"Nothing against Chuck [Oliver] at all. I couldn't do two shows as successfully as he did for that long," noted Chernoff. "When we first started talking about the show, he said he was going to follow my lead. To me, that meant a lot. When presented on his end, he had a lot of trust in me to guide things until he got back into it. It didn't take long to get comfortable."

Change is never easy. After twenty-five years of a proven product, it's not just the talent adjusting to a new environment. It's also the longtime listeners of 680 The Fan adjusting to new expectations after Chuck & Chernoff delivered a familiar afternoon routine for so many years.

For Chernoff, the program with Kincade represents a fresh beginning. He can build on the foundation established through his work with Chuck Oliver while adding a fresh coat of paint with a new yet familiar voice in afternoons.

"We don't do well with change in general. There's going to be people who are hesitant because Chuck & Chernoff was part of their routine. But I sincerely hope that they give it a chance if they're on the fence," said Chernoff. "I've always taken pride in the fact that I can work with different people. I don't want this show to sound like Chuck & Chernoff because that chapter is closed. I don't want to do the same kind of show working with a different partner."

A second chapter is a rarity in sports radio. Chernoff says he understands the unique opportunity he's been given when so many of his peers across the country aren't allowed to try. That's the driving force behind his motivation to build Kincade & Chernoff and reach the heights of his previous program.

"I'm fortunate to build a second show. I talk to so many people and they ask how long I want to do this. As long as I can because I love doing this," explained Chernoff. "If it works like I think it could work for a second time, that would be the biggest feather in the cap to do it a second time around."

That opportunity requires trust and investment from the executives who oversee 680 The Fan. Dickey Broadcasting, which owns 680 The Fan, has been based in Atlanta for nearly 35 years, operating three radio stations and three regional sports networks.

Chernoff considers the opportunity to work for Dickey Broadcasting a blessing. He says the company's continued investment is the biggest key to navigating future success in an evolving content ecosystem.

"Anyone who works in this industry knows what is going on. Working for this company, there's still such an investment in radio. Nothing makes me more proud than that. We invest the way we do as an independent radio station in an era of downsizing or shifting to some sort of AI to avoid costs," said Chernoff. "That's what separates us in the industry. There's an obvious mission to make sure radio has its proper place and investing to back it up."

For twenty-five years, Matt Chernoff and Chuck Oliver gave Atlanta sports fans a place to spend their afternoons. The voices may have changed, but the connection to the audience is what Chernoff believes matters most.

The end of Chuck & Chernoff closed one of the longest-running chapters in Atlanta sports radio. Now, Chernoff has the opportunity to write another one.

There are no guarantees that Kincade & Chernoff will reach the same heights. Building that kind of chemistry takes time, and no second act can simply recreate what made the first one special. Chernoff understands that. He also understands that the opportunity itself is rare.

After a quarter-century behind the microphone, he could have looked back at what he and Oliver accomplished and considered the story complete. Instead, he chose to look forward.

For Chernoff, the goal isn't to replace Chuck & Chernoff . It's to create something that eventually stands on its own.

And if the first twenty-five years taught him anything, it's that the best radio relationships aren't built overnight. They're built one conversation, one laugh and one listener at a time.

articles.title: Warriors news: 'All the options' are on the table for Stephen Curry extension
articles.summary: There may be a lot of uncertainties in the world, but one thing is extremely clear for the Golden State Warriors: They want Stephen Curry. The Warriors are...
articles.body:
There may be a lot of uncertainties in the world, but one thing is extremely clear for the Golden State Warriors : They want Stephen Curry .

The Warriors are bullish on signing Curry to a contract extension, but the two-time MVP does not want it to be a distraction in the upcoming season. He wants to focus on regaining his form and conditioning after getting derailed by multiple injuries last season.

According to ESPN's Shams Charania, Golden State has already presented multiple offers to 38-year-old Curry.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"The ball, according to one Warriors source to me this week, is totally in Stephen Curry 's court. They've given him a slew of options to take. He's got one-year deals, two-year deals, max deals. He's got slightly under the max, where he would be giving the team a discount, some more flexibility. He's got player-option deals as well. So he's got all the options," said Charania.

"But another option that Steph Curry has, not contractually right now, is potentially waiting into the season or waiting until next offseason when the Warriors, if Steph Curry waits, would have about $100 million in cap space."

According to ESPN's Anthony Slater, Curry said he wants "no drama" regarding his contract extension. He stressed that his decision will come at the "right time," noting that helping the Warriors remain competitive is his priority.

The four-time champion, who is entering his 18th season, is eligible for a contract extension of up to two years worth $136.7 million.

Last season, he averaged 26.6 points, 3.6 rebounds, 4.7 assists, and 1.1 steals in 43 games.

"Stephen Curry will be finishing his career in a Golden State uniform," added Charania.

articles.title: Robert Saleh Makes Blunt 49ers Admission About Giants’ Cam Skattebo
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers get a lot of flak for their drafting ability, and some of that is earned. However, they do have an eye for talent, and head coach Kyl...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers get a lot of flak for their drafting ability, and some of that is earned. However, they do have an eye for talent, and head coach Kyle Shanahan nearly had an interesting running back at his disposal.

Christian McCaffrey is that Swiss Army knife that Shanahan uses in the run and passing game, but he nearly had a bruising complementary piece to go alongside him. On Sept. 23, former 49ers defensive coordinator and now Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh admitted that the Niners were keen on Cam Skattebo at last year's draft.

"[Skattebo is] cool, man," Saleh told reporters. "I like him. He's like the old-school 2010 Madden hit stick. Lower your shoulder, run people over. Plays his ass off. Lots of energy. I know going into the draft we were actually about to draft him in San Francisco .

"Kyle loved him, and he ended up getting taken right before we were picking, and I think we ended up with CJ West, who was a pretty damn good player too. He's a spark plug."

Skattebo would be taken in the fourth round, 105th overall, by the New York Giants , and the Niners would pick CJ West in the fourth round a few picks later at 113th overall.

In his two seasons with the Giants , Skattebo has had 131 carries for 527 yards and has scored eight touchdowns in 10 games, per StatMuse . Last season, the second-year running back played only eight games after a right ankle injury cut his campaign short.

49ers' CJ West Goes on Injured Reserve as Depth Is Tested

This year, the 49ers drafted a running back when they selected Kaelon Black in the third round, 90th overall. Moreover, some felt that San Francisco reached for Black, but perhaps Shanahan learned from last year that waiting a few more spots for a draft prospect he likes might come back to bite him.

Speaking of West, the second-year defensive lineman was placed on injured reserve after suffering a bone chip in his knee. Despite being out on injured reserve, the 49ers appear hopeful that they can get him back later in the season.

Nonetheless, the depth at defensive tackle is being tested, and the season is barely three weeks old. Shanahan recently spoke about the concerning situation that he faces on the defensive line.

"Any time you have five defensive tackles make the team, and you're down to two of them through two games, that's always a concern for anybody," Shanahan said (h/t Niners Nation ). "We were able to sign one new guy, and we've got three guys on practice squad that'll be competing to see who is up. We've got guys that are in this building. We've got to see how those guys step it up."

Niners Reporter Gets Blunt on DeForest Buckner Speculation

With the depth being tested, there's been speculation regarding whether the 49ers could bring back Indianapolis Colts ' DeForest Buckner. Nonetheless, 49ers reporter Jennifer Lee Chan of NBC Sports Bay Area said a potential Buckner reunion wouldn't happen right now, despite the Colts being 0-2.

"The Colts have a chance, though," Lee Chan said in a Sept. 22 livestream on her YouTube channel . "Their division is weak. It's too early to let him go. When it comes to being closer to the trade deadline, if the Colts are having a s—-y season, then yes. Maybe they'll trade away [Buckner] because why not at this point? But it's not going to be now.

"It's going to be way closer to the trade deadline. The Niners have to be really playing well and need one piece, and that would have to be [Buckner] and then the Colts have to just be sucking."

articles.title: Alabama Just Lost Two Defensive Playmakers Before South Carolina Game
articles.summary: Alabama will be without two key pieces of its defensive front when South Carolina comes to Bryant-Denny Stadium on Saturday. The Crimson Tide’s first availab...
articles.body:
Alabama will be without two key pieces of its defensive front when South Carolina comes to Bryant-Denny Stadium on Saturday.

The Crimson Tide 's first availability report of the week revealed that edge rushers Justin Hill and Desmond Umeozulu have both been ruled out for the Week 4 matchup.

That could force Alabama to lean more heavily on less-experienced edge players as the Crimson Tide prepares for another SEC test.

Alabama will be without Justin Hill and Desmond Umeozulu

Hill practiced Tuesday and was made available to the media afterward, but the sophomore is dealing with a lower-extremity injury. According to Yea Alabama , Hill is expected to miss a few weeks.

Hill has served as Alabama's backup Wolf linebacker behind Yhonzae Pierre , giving the Crimson Tide another option in its outside linebacker rotation.

Umeozulu's absence is particularly notable given the timing of the matchup. The senior transferred to Alabama from South Carolina and started against Florida State last Saturday, playing a season-high 31 defensive snaps, according to Pro Football Focus .

Umeozulu is dealing with turf toe, according to sources , and his return timeline remains undetermined. Alabama lists him as a co-starter at Bandit on its depth chart.

With both players unavailable, Alabama could turn to Jah-Marien Latham and Fatutoa Henry for additional depth on the edge.

The timing isn't ideal for the Crimson Tide. Alabama is coming off a 50-36 victory over Florida State in which the defense allowed 471 total yards, including 377 through the air.

At the same time, there is some positive injury news. Running backs Daniel Hill and EJ Crowell, along with wide receiver Noah Rogers and running back AK Dear, were not listed on the initial availability report.

Alabama enters the matchup ranked No. 8 nationally at 3-0, while South Carolina is 2-1. The Crimson Tide and Gamecocks are scheduled to kick off at 6 p.m. CT Saturday at Bryant-Denny Stadium on ESPN.

For Alabama, the biggest question now may be how the defensive front responds to losing two players who were expected to contribute to the edge rotation.

articles.title: Containing Avery Johnson is top priority for Bearcats vs. Kansas State
articles.summary: Here's what you need to know before the Cincinnati Bearcats host the Kansas State Wildcats to open Big 12 play.
articles.body:
The University of Cincinnati Bearcats host Kansas State for the season's Big 12 opener Sept. 26 at Nippert Stadium and it'll be the last of four September games played at or near campus to start the season.

It's also the second "Nipp at Night" in the three games played at the historic venue, with last weekend's Victory Bell win over the Miami RedHawks coming at TQL Stadium , a little over two miles from the UC campus.

Both teams enter the game 3-0, with the Bearcats recording wins over Boston College, Western Carolina and Miami University. Kansas State has had three straight wins at Bill Snyder Family Stadium in Manhattan, Kansas, over Nicholls, Washington State and Tulane.

UC leads the all-time series 4-3, but hasn't won since 1966. Kansas State last played at Nippert over 31 years ago and spoiled an upset win by Rick Minter's crew with a last-second touchdown pass . The last two games have been in Manhattan, with the Wildcats winning handily in 2024, 41-15.

Current dual-threat quarterback Avery Johnson passed for two touchdowns and ran for another in that game. In his most recent game vs. Tulane, he threw for 227 yards and ran for 152 with two scores.

"Once he hits the sideline, he is fast-fast," UC Bearcats coach Scott Satterfield said. "He's a different speed. Even like a quarterback that can move and run, he's a little bit better. We have to do a really good job to contain the perimeter runs. They hurt us with that in '24 and he's still doing that now, getting outside and making some big-time runs."

It should be another interesting duel for UC quarterback JC French IV, who threw for 309 yards and two touchdowns vs. Miami's RedHawks and ran for another score. Johnson has six touchdown passes to five for French, but has thrown two interceptions while French has been clean. Johnson has more rushing yards, but French leads in rushing touchdowns 4-3.

"They have a lot of talent on that (Kansas State) defense," French said. "Their stats speak for themselves. They're really good and we're going to have to be on-point with our preparation and obviously go execute this Saturday."

Said Satterfield, "From this point forward, you can't start like that (down 28-7 vs. Miami U.), or it will not end good for us. We've got to come out and play much better early in the game and at the same time finishing in the second half."

Cincinnati Bearcats national recognition

The Bearcats had two players on the Pro Football Focus Big 12 Team of the Week with left guard Evan Tengesdahl and linebacker Jonathan Thompson getting the honors.

On Pro Football Network, right guard Judea Milon has graded out at No. 1 through three weeks at his position at 95.5, with center Taran Tyo No. 4 at 94.9. Right tackle Xavier Lozowicki comes in at No. 6 at 90.7.

However, Kansas State's offensive line also has high marks as the top group through three weeks at 98.9, while UC's pancake men are No. 16 overall in FBS. Kansas State quarterback Johnson had the sixth-best ranking from Week 3 games with his performance in their win over Tulane. Johnson had 152 of the team's 201 rushing yards.

Photos: Cincinnati Bearcats host Miami RedHawks at TQL Stadium

Cincinnati Bearcats vs. Kansas State Wildcats scouting report

The Big 12 hasn't done an official media poll the last two seasons, but in an unofficial tally organized by beat writers around the league, Kansas State was picked eighth and UC 11th.

The Wildcats went from 9-4 in 2024 to 6-6 last season. In December, Collin Klein was hired from Texas A&M, where he was offensive coordinator. Klein is also a former Heisman finalist quarterback at Kansas State.

Why UC has an advantage: There's no place like home, and the Bearcats have won 40 of 56 night home games since 2006. The weather has cooled some and the crowd should be excited to see a team that's averaging nearly 44 points per game. UC's averaging almost 270 yards rushing and 222 yards through the air.

French has taken what he's been given; JV Gibson has a touchdown reception in each game, and running backs Cole Tabb and Gi'Bran Payne have had electric runs.

"Cole's had a huge impact on our team the first three weeks," Satterfield said. "He caught some great throws (vs. Miami). He's a big play threat. If he gets the ball in his hands, he can make people miss, but he also runs through tackles. He's low to the ground and has a really good skill set. Each and every week he just warrants more touches."

Why Kansas State has an advantage : Avery Johnson is the toughest dual-threat the Bearcats have faced thus far and now he's being coached by a former quarterback (Klein). At 6-foot-3 and 200 pounds, he's bigger than the scramblers UC saw vs. Boston College and Western Carolina. Over the past two seasons, he's thrown 47 touchdowns with 16 interceptions, while French had 37 touchdowns with 18 interceptions.

"I'm going to attempt to go get him," UC nose tackle Josh Hough said of Johnson. "I hear he's really fast, but that's not going to stop me from chasing the ball."

Jaron Tibbs and Josh Manning are both 6-foot-3 and have 28 receptions between them. It could be a scorefest as Kansas State averages over 45 points, but Big 12 competition should take the offensive numbers down a peg on both sides.

"This will be a great matchup to watch," Satterfield said. "Normal fans like to watch all the skill guys, but this game, watch the D-linemen vs. the O-line. It's going to be incredible to see. If we can live up to what we're supposed to do up front, that can have a huge impact on this game."

Local connections: Kamari Burns was on UC's defensive line before going to Kansas State in the portal. He has five tackles and 1.5 tackles for loss for the Wildcats. Koy Beasley, from La Salle High School, is second on the team in tackles with 12 at safety. Beasley has also played at Purdue and Miami University.

Cincinnati Bearcats, Kansas State injury updates

Now that Big 12 play has arrived, both schools will have their initial player availability reports out by Wednesday evening, Sept. 23.

Numbers for Cincinnati Bearcats night games at Nippert Stadium

Since 2006, the Bearcats are 40-16 under the lights at home.

"I like 'Nipp at Night'," UC cornerback Kenny Worthy said. "The energy is unmatched, like nothing I've ever been in before. The fans show up every time, they come with full force every time."

UC leads the all-time series 4-3, but hasn't won since 1966. Kansas State last played at Nippert over 31 years ago and spoiled an upset win by Rick Minter's crew with a last-second touchdown pass . The last two games have been in Manhattan, with the Wildcats winning handily in 2024, 41-15.

Current dual-threat quarterback Avery Johnson passed for two touchdowns and ran for another in that game. In his most recent game vs. Tulane, he threw for 227 yards and ran for 152 with two scores.

"Once he hits the sideline, he is fast-fast," UC Bearcats coach Scott Satterfield said. "He's a different speed. Even like a quarterback that can move and run, he's a little bit better. We have to do a really good job to contain the perimeter runs. They hurt us with that in '24 and he's still doing that now, getting outside and making some big-time runs."

It should be another interesting duel for UC quarterback JC French IV, who threw for 309 yards and two touchdowns vs. Miami's RedHawks and ran for another score. Johnson has six touchdown passes to five for French, but has thrown two interceptions while French has been clean. Johnson has more rushing yards, but French leads in rushing touchdowns 4-3.

"They have a lot of talent on that (Kansas State) defense," French said. "Their stats speak for themselves. They're really good and we're going to have to be on-point with our preparation and obviously go execute this Saturday."

Said Satterfield, "From this point forward, you can't start like that (down 28-7 vs. Miami U.), or it will not end good for us. We've got to come out and play much better early in the game and at the same time finishing in the second half."

Cincinnati Bearcats national recognition

The Bearcats had two players on the Pro Football Focus Big 12 Team of the Week with left guard Evan Tengesdahl and linebacker Jonathan Thompson getting the honors.

On Pro Football Network, right guard Judea Milon has graded out at No. 1 through three weeks at his position at 95.5, with center Taran Tyo No. 4 at 94.9. Right tackle Xavier Lozowicki comes in at No. 6 at 90.7.

However, Kansas State's offensive line also has high marks as the top group through three weeks at 98.9, while UC's pancake men are No. 16 overall in FBS. Kansas State quarterback Johnson had the sixth-best ranking from Week 3 games with his performance in their win over Tulane. Johnson had 152 of the team's 201 rushing yards.

Photos: Cincinnati Bearcats host Miami RedHawks at TQL Stadium

Cincinnati Bearcats vs. Kansas State Wildcats scouting report

The Big 12 hasn't done an official media poll the last two seasons, but in an unofficial tally organized by beat writers around the league, Kansas State was picked eighth and UC 11th.

The Wildcats went from 9-4 in 2024 to 6-6 last season. In December, Collin Klein was hired from Texas A&M, where he was offensive coordinator. Klein is also a former Heisman finalist quarterback at Kansas State.

Why UC has an advantage: There's no place like home, and the Bearcats have won 40 of 56 night home games since 2006. The weather has cooled some and the crowd should be excited to see a team that's averaging nearly 44 points per game. UC's averaging almost 270 yards rushing and 222 yards through the air.

French has taken what he's been given; JV Gibson has a touchdown reception in each game, and running backs Cole Tabb and Gi'Bran Payne have had electric runs.

"Cole's had a huge impact on our team the first three weeks," Satterfield said. "He caught some great throws (vs. Miami). He's a big play threat. If he gets the ball in his hands, he can make people miss, but he also runs through tackles. He's low to the ground and has a really good skill set. Each and every week he just warrants more touches."

Why Kansas State has an advantage : Avery Johnson is the toughest dual-threat the Bearcats have faced thus far and now he's being coached by a former quarterback (Klein). At 6-foot-3 and 200 pounds, he's bigger than the scramblers UC saw vs. Boston College and Western Carolina. Over the past two seasons, he's thrown 47 touchdowns with 16 interceptions, while French had 37 touchdowns with 18 interceptions.

"I'm going to attempt to go get him," UC nose tackle Josh Hough said of Johnson. "I hear he's really fast, but that's not going to stop me from chasing the ball."

Jaron Tibbs and Josh Manning are both 6-foot-3 and have 28 receptions between them. It could be a scorefest as Kansas State averages over 45 points, but Big 12 competition should take the offensive numbers down a peg on both sides.

"This will be a great matchup to watch," Satterfield said. "Normal fans like to watch all the skill guys, but this game, watch the D-linemen vs. the O-line. It's going to be incredible to see. If we can live up to what we're supposed to do up front, that can have a huge impact on this game."

Local connections: Kamari Burns was on UC's defensive line before going to Kansas State in the portal. He has five tackles and 1.5 tackles for loss for the Wildcats. Koy Beasley, from La Salle High School, is second on the team in tackles with 12 at safety. Beasley has also played at Purdue and Miami University.

Cincinnati Bearcats, Kansas State injury updates

Now that Big 12 play has arrived, both schools will have their initial player availability reports out by Wednesday evening, Sept. 23.

Since 2006, the Bearcats are 40-16 under the lights at home.

"I like 'Nipp at Night'," UC cornerback Kenny Worthy said. "The energy is unmatched, like nothing I've ever been in before. The fans show up every time, they come with full force every time."
