articles.title: Giants news: Derek Carr turns down social media overature to join NY after Jaxson Dart injury
articles.summary: The New York Giants are searching for an answer at quarterback after Jaxson Dart’s injury, but one retired signal caller has already ruled himself out. Form...
articles.body:
The New York Giants are searching for an answer at quarterback after Jaxson Dart's injury , but one retired signal caller has already ruled himself out. Former Raiders and Saints quarterback Derek Carr responded to an ML Football post asking whether the Giants should try to convince him to come out of retirement and play for the team. The post featured a picture of Carr in New York Giants attire. Carr immediately turned down the hypothetical.

"Beautiful picture but I'm too busy trying to find a level 40 crew to join," he quipped on his X account, referencing NBA 2K.

Fans were astonished that Carr plays the popular NBA 2K franchise, and the Giants now look to other options to fill their need at quarterback. Under new head coach John Harbaugh, Dart was expected to have a breakout season, and by all accounts, Dart was preparing to put together an interesting run.

In the team's Week 1 primetime battle against the rival New York Giants, Dart finished the game with 230 yards and three touchdowns on 23 of 29 attempts and added 11 carries for 54 yards. The numbers led many to believe the young quarterback was ready to turn the Giants into an NFC contender.

But the former Ole Miss standout suffered an injury in the Giants' Monday Night Football matchup against the Los Angeles Rams , as he suffered a knee injury, suffering damage to his MCL, PCL, and meniscus. The injury will ultimately require surgery, and he'll miss the rest of the regular season.

Now, Jameis Winston is back in the spotlight as he steps in as the Giants' starter heading into Week 3.

The Arizona Cardinals made things official with cornerback Will Johnson . He suffered a neck injury on Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks in their 31-7 loss, and he might miss the rest of the season.

They placed him on injured reserve officially on Wednesday. The prognosis remains the same.

"We're bracing for the worst right there," head coach Mike LaFleur said on Wednesday. "I don't know if that's exactly the wording of it, but we're not prepared to have him back if that is."

Replacing him on the roster is cornerback Star Thomas V, who was signed from the practice squad.

Thomas hasn't played since 2024, missing the 2025 season with a torn ACL. He started 15 games in 2024.

What will help is if Garrett Williams can be ready to make his 2026 debut. Max Melton has a toe injury and did not practice Wednesday. Without him, the Cardinals have Denzel Burke , Williams, Thomas, Kei'Trel Clark and Kalen King on the roster. `

ROCHESTER, Ill. (WCIA) -- A 5-0 start to the season and wins over a pair of 7A schools Moline and Rochester has helped Rochester rise to the top of the Class 4A media poll.

"We beat two great teams, a good MacArthur team, so that gives us a lot of confidence, but we've got to keep going," senior wide receiver and safety Nate Swaney said.

And yet, there's still room for improvement.

"We got to be a little bit more consistent," head coach Derek Leonard said. "Every game has had its ups and downs, even the Batavia game, we were probably much better in the first half." "To be state champs and be the best team you can be, you gotta play the whole game."

Senior quarterback JP Leonard's been at the forefront of the strong start, taking over as full-time QB 1 after sharing first-team reps last season.

He's thrown for 13 touchdowns and just one interception.

"He's just a good kid… does things the right way, and it really couldn't have been a better person," Derek Leonard said. "He's worked so hard, and he's nice to everybody… no drama." "He's the perfect quarterback off the field… just leadership and everything." "On the field, this year he's taken a step up like most of our kids do from junior to senior year."

JP credits his supporting cast for his progression.

Five Rockets have at least 100 all-purpose yards over four games played.

"You can't ask for better people on our team," JP Leonard said. "They're super unselfish... they just want to win, and that's all that matters." "They could have ten catches one game, they could have one catch another game, and they're going to be humble." "They're just going to want what's best for their team, so that makes my job a lot easier that they're not coming up to me asking for the ball."

Rochester hopes to keep it's high-powered offense that's scoring over 42 points per game humming in our Friday Football Fever Spotlight Game of the Week at Glenwood.

These teams played an instant classic that Rochester won 43-42 in overtime in 2025 on the way to a 10-1 record and a second-place finish at state.

articles.title: NC State’s CJ Bailey Finally Explains the Play Every Wolfpack Fan Wants to Forget
articles.summary: The NC State Wolfpack were six seconds away from celebrating one of college football’s biggest upsets before a disastrous final play handed Vanderbilt an imp...
articles.body:
The NC State Wolfpack were six seconds away from celebrating one of college football's biggest upsets before a disastrous final play handed Vanderbilt an improbable victory.

Four days later, quarterback CJ Bailey finally addressed the fumble that turned a 31-28 lead into a devastating 35-31 defeat. His explanation revealed what he was thinking during a moment that will be difficult for Wolfpack fans to forget.

Speaking with reporters Wednesday via 247 Sports, Bailey acknowledged his mistake while attempting to explain why he continued moving around the end zone instead of simply securing the football.

The quarterback described his competitive mentality and desire to exhaust the remaining clock. However, that explanation raises an interesting question about whether his instincts ultimately worked against what NC State needed most.

CJ Bailey Explains What Went Wrong Against Vanderbilt

"I was just trying to get all the clock out," Bailey said. "The biggest thing was just holding the ball, bro. I know that's the biggest thing. I was just trying to run around and make a play. I'm a competitive guy. I was just competing until the final second."

Bailey's explanation came after one of the most remarkable endings of the college football season. NC State held a three-point lead with six seconds remaining and possession near its own goal line. Coach Dave Doeren called for an intentional safety designed to exhaust the clock while preserving the Wolfpack's lead.

Instead, Vanderbilt defensive lineman Miles Capers stripped Bailey in the end zone, and Cayden Daniels recovered the football for the winning touchdown. The Commodores completed a comeback from a 17-point deficit, leaving NC State searching for answers after a game it had controlled for most of the afternoon.

Bailey also addressed the instructions he received before the play, explaining that there had been considerable communication but that he had never experienced that exact situation in a game. He acknowledged the outcome rather than attempting to shift responsibility elsewhere.

"I fumbled the ball," Bailey said. "It is what it is. I got to move forward."

NC State's Final-Play Mistake Raises Questions Beyond CJ Bailey

Perhaps the most frustrating part for NC State fans is that Bailey had already done enough to put his team in position to win. He completed 25 of 37 passes for 275 yards and three touchdowns against Vanderbilt, connecting with Keenan Jackson for all three scores. Unfortunately, his final mistake overshadowed an otherwise productive afternoon.

His competitive mentality is understandable, but the final play required something considerably different from an ordinary offensive possession. NC State did not need another explosive play or an extraordinary individual effort. The objective was to exhaust the remaining seconds, protect the football and, if necessary, surrender two points.

Doeren has also acknowledged responsibility for the decision, explaining that his coaching staff regularly practices similar late-game situations. That distinction matters because Bailey was executing a designed play, even if his failure to protect the football ultimately proved decisive.

Now, Bailey faces the challenge of recovering from a mistake that attracted attention throughout the football world. NC State hosts Appalachian State on Saturday, giving its quarterback an immediate opportunity to respond.

There is no changing what happened in Nashville . Bailey can only ensure that one disastrous moment does not become the defining story of his season.

While the final fumble was a disaster , NC State's loss was driven by a defensive collapse that allowed 21 fourth-quarter points and surrendered massive touchdown passes of 33 and 43 yards. That's an important fact that college football and NC State fans need to understand while analyzing what transpired.

articles.title: Warriors Get Major Update on Brandin Podziemski’s Future
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors have a big decision to make on Brandin Podziemski, who will be a restricted free agent next summer. The post Warriors Get Major Upd...
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors have a big decision to make on Brandin Podziemski , who will be a restricted free agent next summer.

NBA insider Tim MacMahon fears the Warriors and Podz may be far apart on a realistic number for a contract extension, citing the guard's "delusional" sense of self-worth.

"I'm curious about what Brandin Podziemski thinks he should be paid," MacMahon said on the latest "Hoop Collective" podcast, via Basket Ball Network.

"Because this is a guy that's said some crazy things, like he thinks he can be better than Steph and like some ridiculous things that are just completely separated from reality."

In fairness to Podz, he had a bounce-back season last year after an underwhelming sophomore campaign. The southpaw averaged a career-high 13.8 points and 3.7 assists while playing all 82 games (43 starts) for Steve Kerr's team. He also averaged 1.1 steals per game, earning praise from his teammates for his activity on defense.

Despite a solid season, Podz rubbed a lot of people ( including teammate Draymond Green ) wrong with some of his comments last year. Notably, he expressed confidence about leading the Warriors into a new era when Stephen Curry and Green ride off into the sunset, after previously anointing himself as Curry's successor.

MacMahon feels the outspoken Podz may pay the price for his past comments.

"To succeed in the NBA, a lot of guys need ot have a delusional sense of confidence. I'm not holding it against him," MacMahon said of the fourth-year Warriors guard.

"I'm just saying, in terms of negotiations, I don't think you can pay a deal like Ausar Thompson just got or like Keyonte George just got."

Some have urged the Warriors trade Podz beforehand to avoid a Jonathan Kuminga -like situation. In the 2025 offseason, the Warriors and Kuminga endured a painstaking contract negotiation that ended with the Congolese forward signing a two-year deal. However, he was shipped off to the Atlanta Hawks midseason.

The Warriors may also prefer to lock up Podz to a longterm deal before he hits restricted free agency, like they did with Moses Moody a few years ago.

Podz, though, may ultimately prove a lot of naysayers wrong and enjoy a productive career after all. ESPN's Zach Kram has projected the southpaw to make a big leap this season and establish himself as Golden State's full-time starting shooting guard.

"Podziemski is underrated because he's a jack of all trades, master of none," Kram wrote last week. "He was one of 13 players last season to average at least five rebounds and three assists while making at least 37% of his 3s; those other 12 include 10 players in our Top 100, the underrated Okongwu and Kyshawn George , who was another player I considered for this list of players to watch.

"Even if Podziemski is unlikely ever to develop into a star, his all-around solid play makes him a valuable contributor. He can make open 3s, support Stephen Curry with secondary playmaking and hold his own on the defensive end. Even a moderate improvement in his age-23 season should place him firmly in Top 100 consideration next year."

articles.title: Scammer Posing as Pittsburgh Steelers Player Eli Heidenreich Conned Women Out of $1000
articles.summary: The two victims are a 20-year-old woman and a 50-year-old woman from Avella, Penn.
articles.body:
Two women in Pennsylvania were scammed by someone posing as Pittsburgh Steelers player Eli Heidenreich

Police say the scam involved multiple financial transactions, costing the women $1,000

No suspects have been named, and the Pennsylvania State Police are asking the public for information

Two women were scammed by someone impersonating Pittsburgh Steelers rookie Eli Heidenreich.

The 20-year-old woman and the 50-year-old woman from Avella, Penn., were scammed out of $1,000 in July by a person who claimed to be the Steelers running back, according to a Pennsylvania State Police public information report viewed by PEOPLE.

The report says the scam involved several financial transactions. Police said no suspects have been identified, and asked the public to contact them with any relevant information.

Want to keep up with the latest crime coverage? Sign up for PEOPLE's free True Crime newsletter for breaking crime news, ongoing trial coverage and details of intriguing unsolved cases.

Heidenreich, a Pittsburgh native, was the 230th overall pick during the 2026 NFL Draft, chosen by the Pittsburgh Steelers. He has not yet played in an NFL game, per the team's website .

PEOPLE reached out to representatives for Eli Heidenreich and the Pennsylvania State Police for comment.

The incident involving Heidenreich's persona comes after two men allegedly posed as a 49ers player and his financial advisor to scam people out of $1.3 million. In late August, Daejon Labrayae Love, 35, and Taylor Jamie Chan, 18, were charged with wire fraud and conspiracy to commit wire fraud, the Department of Justice previously announced .

Prosecutors allege that Love convinced women he met on dating apps that he was a wide receiver for the San Francisco 49ers or a wealthy real estate investor from Switzerland, while Chan posed as his financial advisor.

The scheme allegedly took place over about four years until the pair's arrest and defrauded at least 26 people out of $1.3 million, the Justice Department said.

articles.title: Analyst suggest 49ers trade for former 1st-round WR
articles.summary: The 49ers need receiver support, and they could snag this one at a cheap price.
articles.body:
San Francisco 's wide receiver room has turned into a triage unit, and it's only Week 3.

Rookie De'Zhaun Stribling could miss up to 10 weeks with an ankle injury. Demarcus Robinson went down with a high-ankle sprain in Week 2 that could sideline him for an extended stretch. Ricky Pearsall is already out for the year following knee surgery. Christian Kirk is still on injured reserve with a calf strain. And now Mike Evans , the 49ers ' big free-agent addition, left Sunday's win with a hip injury.

It's not a new problem for Kyle Shanahan's offense. And the remaining stars, George Kittle and Deebo Samuel , have both battled injuries of their own in recent seasons. But this year the position has no cushion left. Beyond Evans and Samuel, the depth chart thins out fast, with unproven names like Jacob Cowing and Jordan Watkins next in line.

That's why Bleacher Report's Moe Moton floated a name worth San Francisco's attention this week: Cleveland Browns wideout Jerry Jeudy .

With a laundry list of injuries at wideout, the 49ers need a long-term fit at the position. Play-calling head coach Kyle Shanahan may be able to resurrect Jerry Jeudy's career. Over the offseason, general manager Andrew Berry called Jeudy the "bell cow" of the Browns' receiver corps, but the seventh-year pro has just two catches for 26 yards in two games. Jeudy didn't record a reception in the Browns' 23-19 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 2. Jeudy is only two years removed from a Pro Bowl year in which he caught 90 passes for 1,229 yards and four touchdowns. Still in his prime, the 27-year-old can be an asset to the 49ers' injury-riddled receiver unit.

articles.title: Alejandra Salazar y Aimar Goñi, las 'patatas calientes' de España para el Mundial de pádel
articles.standfirst: Este jueves a partir de las 13:00 horas los seleccionadores Juanjo Gutiérrez y Carolina Navarro darán a conocer sus 8 elegidos para el Mundial de Doha 2026
articles.summary: Este jueves a partir de las 13:00 horas los seleccionadores Juanjo Gutiérrez y Carolina Navarro darán a conocer sus 8 elegidos para el Mundial de Doha 2026
articles.body: Ha llegado el día. Este jueves a las 13 horas Juanjo Gutiérrez y Carolina Navarro harán públicas sus convocatorias de 8 integrantes para representar a España en el Mundial de pádel 2026 que se celebrará en Doha del 2 al 7 de noviembre. En un acto programado en la capital de España en el Cupra City Garage del centro de Madrid, ambos responsables de los equipos nacionales despejarán las dudas sobre los componentes de la selección, clara aspirante en ambas modalidades a llevarse el título. Por la parte masculina, en busca del que sería el quinto título de su historia -desde 2021 no lo logran- todo parece bastante claro a falta de confirmación, aunque hay un nombre propio que apunta a ser la gran sorpresa: Aimar Goñi. El joven navarro, como ya contó MARCA hace unos meses, es muy del gusto del seleccionador y se postula como cuarto revés de la lista. La otra alternativa es Javi Leal, aunque sobre el papel parte con menos opciones. Y, como cuarto drive, el mejor colocado es Jon Sanz. El navarro ya sabe lo que es jugar un Mundial y sólo el malagueño Fran Guerrero podría desbancarle de una lista que tiene claramente seis fijos: Alejandro Galán, Paquito Navarro y Coki Nieto como jugadores de revés; Arturo Coello, Juan Lebrón y Mike Yanguas como jugadores de derecha. En el femenino, el panorama parece si cabe aún más claro que en el masculino. Con el debut de Carolina Navarro al frente del combinado absoluto, la gran y única incógnita aparece en una de las plazas de jugadoras de drive. Y las dos candidatas son Marta Ortega y Alejandra Salazar. La primera, habitual ya en los últimos triunfos mundialistas de España, está cuajando una temporada muy regular en Premier Padel, demostrando que sigue al máximo nivel con sus dos compañeras de baile hasta ahora: Martina Calvo -que debutará en la lista con solo 18 años- y Sofía Araujo. La segunda, ganadora siete veces del Mundial con España, también ha demostrado a sus 40 años que será competitiva hasta el final de su carrera, que será en tres meses. Su presencia o su ausencia será lo que marque una convocatoria estelar. Las piezas que parecen fijas son Gemma Triay, Ariana Sánchez, Martina Calvo y Bea González como reveses, mientras que para el drive, y a la espera de la decisión entre Ortega o Salazar, estarán Paula Josemaría, Andrea Ustero y Claudia Fernández.

articles.body:
Long before he took on the fight name of "The Handsome White Dragon," Luo Chao was simply an ambitious kid in China navigating the ancient traditions of his homeland.

articles.body:
WEST SACRAMENTO, CA — Athletics catcher Brian Serven left Wednesday's game early after taking a ball to the face.

Serven was at bat in the bottom of the sixth inning when Angels pitcher José Fermin threw a 94 mph changeup that resulted in a foul ball.

The pitch just skimmed Serven's bat, which he had in a bunt position, and ricocheted directly into his left cheek bone, just under his eye. He took the impact and fell to the dirt.

Athletics manager Mark Kotsay and the team trainer ran immediately onto the field to check on Serven as Angels' infielders took a sportsmanship knee. Serven was down for several moments but slowly got up, signaling he was OK.

articles.title: After blood clots and a stroke, Mike Williams returns to Texas and finds old memories
articles.summary: Blood clots cut short Mike Williams' NFL career, and a stroke brought a long recovery. His Texas Athletics Hall of Honor return stirred warm memories for the...
articles.body:
AUSTIN - Mike Williams came home last week.

The former All-American offensive tackle at Texas , who was on the ground floor of the Longhorns ' rebirth as a national power in Mack Brown's first recruiting class, loved every minute of his homecoming.

When he walked into Royal-Memorial Stadium last Friday as one of 13 new inductees into the Texas Athletics Hall of Honor, the warm memories came flooding back, washing over him like a tidal wave of emotions.

He remembered it all from a quarter of a century ago.

Showing up at Texas and curiously recruited as a defensive lineman. Coming to Austin even though he'd made up his mind he was going to Baylor . Recalling the week he and his teammates and coaches struggled to come to grips with the tragic vehicular death of defensive lineman Cole Pittman in 2001. Playing for Mack Brown and loving the family atmosphere the head coach created.

Heck, he still remembers Brown coming to his home and being so comfortable that the coach sat on the floor, his back against the couch. "How could I not go to Texas?" he said.

"It's been 24 years since I was there, and it all came back," said the 46-year-old Texan, who lives in Virginia Beach, Va., with his wife, stepchildren Dawson and Macy and daughter Mia. "The stadium has changed completely. I was driving on campus and told my family this is where I played, that's where I went to class."

When Texas athletic director Chris Del Conte called last June to tell Williams he was to be a part of the 2026 Hall of Honor class that also included fellow football players Lawrence Sampleton, Malcom Brown and Jackson Jeffcoat as well as three-time Olympic gold medalist shot putter Ryan Crouser and four-time All-American softball pitcher Blaire Luna, he asked him if he'd gotten his degree.

Alas, Williams had to admit he hadn't completed his sociology degree with a minor in business. But he will, at least online.

He jokes that he has a niece named Jada and a nephew named Emory who currently go to college at Oklahoma and Texas A&M, respectively. "I failed somewhere," Williams said.

The weekend of festivities, surrounding Texas' win over UTSA on Saturday , rekindled all the heartfelt emotions within him and renewed his perspective.

Williams told the Houston Chronicle that Del Conte kidded him and said Texas can't have a Hall of Honor inductee who didn't have a diploma. That stirred something within the former first-round pick of the Buffalo Bills .

He's long since stepped away from the NFL after four injury-filled seasons with the Bills and a short one-year stint with Washington . His career was cut short by an occurrence of blood clots that led to his retirement.

He has no regrets but with one exception.

"I wish it could have been longer," he said. "Buffalo was great. I love me some Buffalo."

His shortened time there didn't leave him embittered. Instead, it emboldened him to better understand adversity and the need to respond positively. That's a lesson he frequently shares with his 13-year-old daughter Mia, who is a budding wrestling star and is aiming for the 2032 Olympics. He learned from a series of medical setbacks to listen to his body rather than to just push through the pain.

"It taught me a lot that I can impart to Mia," Williams said of his daughter, who took up Brazilian jujitsu at age 7 and was once asked to join her middle-school football team as a running back. "I've told her to be like Wonder Woman. She can be as girly as can be, but when she steps on the mat, her mentality fits her nickname, which is Pit Bull. She is not mean, just hyper-focused."

So was Mike who had more than his share of calamity. It started when he learned he had blood clots in his calf in the 2010 offseason after he'd started eight games for Washington.

His problems began when he started having trouble breathing. His right calf hurt. His heart was racing. He thought about the criticism he received when some said the 6-foot-6, 345-pounder was just out of shape. Typical overweight lineman, some sniped.

"I'd been out of shape before," he said. "But this was different. When you're an athlete, you believe you can almost push through anything that might be debilitating to non-athletes."

When he received the initial diagnosis of deep vein thrombosis, Williams shrugged and said OK. What medicine does he need? Give him a prescription and let him get back to practice. Why the long faces?

Well, the blood clots in his calf had broken free and traveled to his lungs. He was told he was suffering from a pulmonary embolism and would be on blood thinners forever. He'd lost all function of his right side.

That spelled the end of his pro career, but it wasn't the last of his severe medical hardships.

Three years ago, he awoke at 3 a.m. He was sweating profusely. He got up to use the restroom but had trouble seeing. He stood up and immediately felt weakness in the entire right side of his body. He had double vision. The room was spinning.

His wife Jamie asked him what was wrong. Williams shrugged it off and asked for some aspirin. She grew more concerned and convinced him he needed to go to the emergency room. He reluctantly complied.

In the examination room, the attending physician checked out his symptoms and immediately diagnosed the problem

"That's not what you want to hear," Williams said.

He knew he was in for a long recovery. He had trouble walking and had to undergo weeks of physical therapy. He could barely speak.

"I couldn't formulate my words," said Williams, who once suffered from a bad stuttering problem. "I could visualize the words in my brain, but I couldn't get them out."

He's just now weaning himself off the cane that accompanied him for almost three years. The strength in his right side hasn't completely returned. His knee will occasionally give out. But he's returning to good health and counts his blessings.

His time at Texas wasn't always rosy, either.

He told reporters last week that he almost quit the Texas football team during his freshman year. In fact, he might have, had not Longhorn assistant coach Hardee McCrary not taken a personal interest in The Colony graduate whom he and line coach Tim Nunez recruited.

"I almost wanted to quit. True story," Williams said. "I was a freshman, I actually wanted to go home. Mack Brown and all the team were on the field, and Hardee McCrary actually sat there with me and said, 'Hey, don't worry about practice, stay here, let's talk.' It was just kind of like that freshman wall. But the next morning, I got up and I was just fine, and then the rest is history."

A remarkable history, considering he'd never played in the offensive line in high school.

After toggling between the offensive and defensive line as a freshman, as did teammate Leonard Davis, Williams played in the Cotton Bowl win over Mississippi State as the team's fifth defensive lineman before becoming a full-time offensive tackle.

He'll never forget the traumatic death of Pittman, the defensive tackle who died when his pickup truck swerved off the road on U.S. 79 on his return to Austin from his home in Shreveport, La. He can still recall the entire team gathering at midfield at DKR under gray skies and singing "The Eyes of Texas" at practice.

Eight months after the tragedy, the Longhorns opened the season against North Carolina , Brown's former team, and beat the Tar Heels with freshman tailback Cedric Benson scoring his first touchdown. Texas wore a CP decal on its helmets. Brett Robin capped the emotional day when he scored on a 12-yard run with 36 seconds to play to make it 44-14, but quarterback Major Applewhite took a knee instead of running the extra-point try. Pittman's jersey number was 44.

"I remember Cory Redding yelling on the sideline to look at the scoreboard to leave the score," Williams said. "That was meant to be. It was a perfect sendoff for Cole."

And Williams had a full college experience he treasures to this day. He still checks in with teammates like Ahmad Brooks and Lee Jackson and Derrick Dockery. He regularly watches Texas' games but admits it can be "very stressful."

Williams started 28 games for the Longhorns and was a consensus All-American as a senior. He was selected fourth in the 2002 NFL draft, and became one of Texas' 15 top-five draft picks in history.

Many of those memories came back to him last weekend while watching the Longhorns beat the Roadrunners. As he stared down at the field below from the Founders suite at DKR, he was overwhelmed with positive reflections. And a bit of bravado.

"I remembered the feeling and felt I could get out there and play right now," he said. "I was fired up. I think I could give 'em a good five plays. That's just the ballplayer in you. It never goes away."

articles.title: Robert Saleh reveals 49ers were ‘about to draft’ Giants star Cam Skattebo
articles.summary: Robert Saleh has revealed the San Francisco 49ers were “about to draft” New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo before the NFC rivals selected him in the f...
articles.body:
Robert Saleh has revealed the San Francisco 49ers were "about to draft" New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo before the NFC rivals selected him in the fourth round last year.

Saleh, now head coach of the Tennessee Titans , was San Francisco 's defensive coordinator at the time and confirmed that Kyle Shanahan was particularly high on Skattebo.

The Giants eventually took Skattebo with the 105th overall pick, while the 49ers selected defensive lineman C.J. West seven selections later at No. 113.

Robert Saleh reveals how close Cam Skattebo came to joining the 49ers

Speaking to reporters, Saleh explained just how close San Francisco came to adding the bruising running back.

"[Skattebo is] cool, man," Saleh said. "I like him. He's like the old-school 2010 Madden hit stick. Lower your shoulder, run people over. Plays his *** off. Lots of energy. I know going into the draft we were actually about to draft him in San Francisco."

Saleh also revealed that Shanahan was a big admirer of Skattebo before the Giants took him off the board.

"[Kyle] loved him, and he ended up getting taken right before we were picking, and I think we ended up with CJ West, who was a pretty damn good player too. He's a spark plug."

Skattebo has since become an important part of the Giants' offence. Through 10 games, he has recorded 131 carries for 527 yards and eight touchdowns, according to the supplied reference.

His role could become even more important following Jaxson Dart 's season-ending knee injury, with Jameis Winston now taking over at quarterback.

That change could place greater responsibility on Skattebo, particularly after he averaged 4.4 yards per carry with Dart on the field compared with 2.9 without him in the 2026 season, according to Sumer Sports.

The Giants will face Saleh's Titans on Sunday, giving the former 49ers coach a first-hand look at the running back San Francisco nearly drafted.

For Shanahan and the 49ers, Saleh's admission offers another reminder of just how close they came to adding Skattebo to an offence that already featured Christian McCaffrey .

articles.title: Yankees’ Aaron Judge not happy injury details revealed, wants to be ready for playoff opener
articles.summary: Yankees captain Aaron Judge hopes to return from a Grade 2 right calf strain way sooner than the usual six-to-eight week timeline... for next Tuesday's Wild...
articles.body:
NEW YORK — Yankees captain Aaron Judge hasn't given up on being back for the start of the playoffs even though he's very early into recovering from a serious calf injury. He's also not thrilled that his manager revealed his strain is a Grade 2, which typically has a six-to-eight week recovery time.

This drama overshadowed Ben Rice hitting his 40 th and 41 st home runs in Wednesday night's 9-2 Yankees romp over the Rays , who played like they had a hangover a night after clinching the AL East crown at Yankee Stadium.

Judge returned from an 88-game absence with a fractured rib on Sept. 8, then injured his calf eight days later. The Yankees didn't reveal the severity until after Judge was back on injured list. Then, Judge said he planned on returning for the start of the playoffs.

Before Tuesday's game, Boone revealed Judge has a moderate strain, which is a Grade 2. The manager added that he's not expecting Judge back for the first round of the playoffs, but also not ruling it out.

The Grade 2 revelation led to most everyone outside the organization counting Judge out for at least the Wild Card Series and maybe the entire postseason. Before Wednesday's game, Judge repeated his past comments in a short interview with ESPN, saying he planned on being ready for the playoffs. He also hinted that he was upset with Boone making his MRI grade public, saying "I can't control what people say, so you'll have to talk to them about that."

After the Yankees romp, Boone approached a group of media after winning pitcher Gerrit Cole's postgame interview and said, "Got some questions?"

For the next few minutes, Judge repeatedly made it clear that he hopes to come back as soon as he can because he doesn't want to miss playoff games. He also made it clear that he was not happy Boone told the truth about his MRI results.

We didn't necessarily expect you for the first round of the postseason. There is a report that you said today that you expect to be in there. What leads you to believe that you're going to be good to go come Tuesday?

Judge: "My goal is to come back as soon as I can. That's what we're doing right now. If (Boone) says I'm not gonna be ready, I've got no control over that. I've got control over what I can do to try to get back as soon as I can. So if you ask me if I'm gonna be back, I'm gonna tell you yeah, I'm doing everything I can. Every single day I show up here to get back and be ready to go."

What can you tell us about what you have been doing? You had the PPP shot on Monday. Have you done anything since?

Judge: "We're doing some work back there in the training room and weight room. I'm doing everything I can so I can be ready to go when the postseason starts."

Do you feel like you have to be ready to play right field, or would you come back and be able to DH?

Judge: "Any form they need me. Obviously, I want to try to come back and be ready to play the field because I think that gives us the best lineup, especially with how Benny's been swinging the bat. You got Garcia and Goldie at first base. I'm a right fielder. That's what we're trying to do. Anyway I can get back to be in good form to play a good outfield, for sure."

How do you weigh wanting to come back as soon as you can, and the risk involved, especially with that kind of injury with the calf. It can make it potentially worse for the future?

Judge: "I weigh it, and I weigh it like this: We've got a great team, and we've got a great opportunity in front of us. The future is not guaranteed, good or bad. My job is to do whatever I can to get back, and things are feeling great, so that's what I'm trying to do. If you ask if I'm trying to come back and play, of course."

Do you worry that coming back sooner than the recommended timeline could cause further damage?

Judge: "I'm not a doctor. I don't know what's going to happen. I just know how I feel when I wake up in the morning. I evaluate how I'm feeling and I continue to make progress to get back on the field. I can't tell you the future, what that's going to hold. I don't know what's going to happen tonight or the next day, so I just focus on today and try to improve a little bit every single day so when that time comes around for postseason, we're ready to go."

Have the medical people said it's conceivable that you could be a full player by Tuesday night?

Judge: "We're going into the postseason, so I think we're all on board that you've got to get back as soon as we can."

Boone said on Tuesday that it was a moderate calf strain. Usually that takes several weeks to recover. Is it realistic for you to be back by Tuesday?

Judge: "Everybody's moderate's a little different. I think your moderate's a little different than my moderate, and so on and so on. I don't know why (Boone) used those words, but I'm trying to come back as soon as I can."

Do you need to be pain free, or is it a matter of they can tape the calf tightly and you play through it?

Judge: "I think everybody's really banged up. They're all dealing with something. So come back to where I can be a great player for the New York Yankees, that's what we're trying to do."

Are you upset that Boone called it moderate or suggested it was unlikely you'd be able to play in this series?

Judge: "Boonie's my guy, so I've always got his back. I know he makes the right decisions. Obviously as a player you don't want to hear that, but that's out of my control. I've got a job. I've got to come back and be ready to go. And that's what I'm focused on right now."

You mentioned you're working out. Do you have any idea when you may be able to resume baseball activities?

Judge: "I've got to talk to the trainer about that one. I'm not sure. But like I said, we're doing everything in our power to speed this process up. If it happened in May, I think maybe the timeline's a little different and maybe we can give you a timeline and better information, but we've got work to do. That's where we're focused on."

There are still steps though that you have to go through that you probably can't skip, like running the bases. We're seeing Giancarlo Stanton go through that now. Obviously, it's not the same exact injury, but it's a calf injury. Is there a way to speed up the process?

Judge: "It's tough to say. I think each injury is a little different. G's is probably a little different than mine, so we'll see what they got lined up. But like I said, the goal is to be back as soon as possible. I know I'm ruled out for the regular season, but we'll see what happens when the postseason starts."

You've never missed a playoff game. What goes to your head thinking that you might not be part of that series?

Judge: "I haven't really thought about it because I'm focused on what I can do in the next couple days. The Bronx is a magical place in October. Even going back to last year, I know we didn't finish a goal, but it was a great series against Boston in the Wild Card and a tough series against the Blue Jays. I don't want to miss out (this year) on that opportunity."

Do you notice any difference since having the PPP injection on Monday?

Judge: "Any injection doesn't feel too good that day, but I feel a lot better today and we're gonna keep making strides."

articles.title: Prado Grabs SMX Playoff Lead Heading Into The Final
articles.summary: Jorge Prado will enter this weekend’s 450SMX Playoff finally with the lead after taking the overall victory on the back of two runner-up finishes at Playoff...
articles.body:
Anything can happen with triple points available in the final

Jorge Prado will enter this weekend's 450SMX Playoff finally with the lead after taking the overall victory on the back of two runner-up finishes at Playoff 2. Prado's consistency gave him the slim edge over Ken Roczen and Hunter Lawrence, who each earned a moto win and a fourth-place finish. With double points on offer, that small edge added up to a real cushion in the championship chase heading into the Final.

The first 20-minute-plus-one-lap moto belonged to Roczen after a sustained duel with Prado. The Spaniard grabbed the holeshot and led early, trading fast laps with the Progressive Insurance Cycle Gear Suzuki rider before Roczen made an aggressive pass just before halfway and opened a gap of more than two seconds.

Prado clawed it back through lapped traffic and drew within a second on the final lap, but Roczen held on to win by 1.3 seconds. Haiden Deegan took a close third ahead of Lawrence and Cooper Webb.

Moto 2 was the wilder of the two. Lawrence launched his CRF450RWE to the holeshot, briefly ceded the lead to Prado, then reclaimed it and pulled clear, ultimately winning by 14.9 seconds.

Behind him the race for the overall descended into chaos with a four-way tie for the lead in play. Prado went down in the sand at the midpoint and remounted in fourth before charging back past Roczen for third.

An intense battle for second between Prado and Deegan ended when Deegan crashed in the sand. Deegan and Roczen then got tangled on the reentry, Webb slipped past both, and contact during a pass by Deegan put Webb on the ground. Second went to Prado, ahead of Deegan and Roczen.

Under Supermotocross' Olympic scoring system, Prado's 2-2 gave him the lead for the overall victory. Lawrence (4-1) and Roczen (1-4) finished level for second, but Lawrence's win in the second moto broke the tie in his favor. Two moto podiums (3-3) were not enough for Deegan, who came up just short of the box in fourth.

The double points swung the title picture in Prado's favor, moving him 16 points clear of Deegan and Lawrence, who share second. Roczen sits fourth, 18 points back, with Webb (5-5) another two points adrift in fifth.

With triple points up for grabs, anything can happen at the SMX Final, September 26 at Thunder Ridge Nature Arena in Ridgedale, Missouri.

articles.title: Merritt Island wins 5-set classic over Satellite in conference final
articles.summary: Merritt Island and Satellite squared off in an epic Cape Coast Conference Tournament final with the Mustangs rallying from a fifth-set deficit to win.
articles.body:
Merritt Island hosted Satellite on Sept. 23 for the Cape Coast Conference championship in search of its third consecutive title.

Satellite, who had won 10 of its last 12 matches since losing in four sets to Merritt Island on Sept. 1, fought back from two one-set deficits to send the title match to a decisive fifth set.

After falling behind 7-3, Merritt Island surged ahead with a 10-2 run and closed out the match to win 25-21, 16-25, 25-14, 25-27, 15-11.

"Very proud. They had to work for every single point. It was very emotional. A lot on the line, obviously," Merritt Island head coach Angie Patrick said. "It was the perfect setup for a championship because Satellite absolutely brought their A-game. It was just a battle. It was awesome, but I'm really proud of the way the girls came through in the fifth set."

Mustangs, Scorpions clash in conference volleyball finals

Merritt Island thought it had won the match in four sets, but the game-winning kill was called off by the referee on a violation. Satellite scored the next two points to send it to the fifth set.

The Mustangs overcame the fifth-set deficit and tied the match at 9-9 on a kill from junior Ema Michell. Merritt Island closed out the match on 2 kills from senior Bella Becker and 4 kills from junior Lydia Scott, including the final 3 Mustang points.

"That was really up and down. I think we just kind of came in knowing that they really wanted it. We knew that last game they played their hardest that second set," senior setter Amber Ives said. "They did the same. They took that from us, but I think we came out third set with the momentum. They took it from us fourth set. We were down. We fought back. Just high energy all around."

Ives orchestrated the Merritt Island attack and finished the night with a double-double of 67 assists and 25 digs. As one of eight seniors on the roster, Ives said the group was determined to not let the conference title slip away.

"I think we just wanted it so bad," Ives said. "We haven't dropped a Cape Coast Conference to them and we just trusted each other and just ran our stuff and we got it."

Scott and Michell put Merritt Island on their backs as the focal point of the attack. Scott spiked a career-high 29 kills to go with 14 digs, 2 aces and 1 block. She surpassed her previous career-high of 28 set on Sept. 15 in a five-set win at Bishop Moore.

Michell ended the match with 15 kills, 3 blocks and 1 ace. She also played a pivotal role in the back row defending the Satellite attack with 22 digs.

"You don't win games like that without those two. They just have done a great job for us," Patrick said. "It's hard when there's so much put on their shoulders. They're starting to really mature and handle that. Our team needs that."

Ives increased her assists season total to 403. The senior is close to surpassing last season's total of 479. After beginning the season in a 6-2 formation, Ives has been the primary setter in the new 5-1 formation in recent matches.

"I've come a long way. I've really worked on my tempo," Ives said. "We started running a 5-1 and the coaches really put a lot of trust in me with that. I just want to prove myself through that."

Merritt Island took home its 25th conference title in school history. Becker and junior Gena Walters finished with 10 and 8 kills, respectively. Sophomore Sadie Hesse tallied 4 kills.

The Mustangs improved to 13-3 and they'll host Titusville on Sept. 28. All three losses have come to teams in the top nine of the FHSAA rankings. The most recent coming in a three-set tournament defeat to North Broward Prep on Sept. 19 in a rematch of last year's state championship match.

"We just got to monitor our bodies and our health and take care of ourselves. Mentally, I think we're super dialed in. We're coming to practice and working hard.," Patrick said. "I'm really excited what's going to come. We're going to have a great PINK Tournament. We got a big game next with a region opponent, so we'll see how that goes and keep it rolling."

Since 2007, Satellite entered the match having lost 30 straight matches to Merritt Island. For the first time during that stretch, the Scorpions were able to push the Mustangs to five sets.

"I'm not into moral victories, but I'm into how my team plays. It's not judged by the score in every match. It's judged by our effort, our energy," Satellite head coach Daren Bolton said. "My bench, my JV, my freshman team, our fans, our team on the floor, they played inspired volleyball. Never laid down. We had the opportunity to quit, but we didn't quit."

After dropping the first set, Satellite broke a 12-12 tie in the second set with a 6-0 run and never looked back. The Scorpions forced the fifth set on a kill by sophomore Kenzie Little and an ace from senior Lily Ruda.

They built an early advantage in the fifth set on 4 kills from sophomore Harper Lanza, 1 kill from Ruda and an ace serve from junior Lily Sigety.

"We were better in all phases of the game, especially serving," Bolton said. "If we play like we did (tonight), we're going to have a long season."

Little and Lanza led the Scorpions with 17 and 16 kills, respectively, but other players stepped up and contributed. In the middle, senior Kirra Snyder and junior Macy Ferland combined for 7 kills and 6 blocks. Ruda tallied 3 aces to go with 2 kills. Sigety and Lanza split the setting while sophomore Cady Tinch dug balls all night in the back row.

"(Little and Lanza) played phenomenal, but it was our supporting cast. Our defense, our passing, our setting, our serving," Bolton said. "We could have had a few more blocks, turn a few touches into blocks and that might have been the difference, but when you're in a game against a good program like that, it's exciting."

Satellite dropped to 13-5 and it'll host Bayside on Sept. 28. Bolton said he hopes the team's performance instills more confidence heading into the final five matches of the season.

"We got some games that we got to take care of business," Bolton said. "We got to make sure our ranking is good enough so we can host districts and playoffs. We got a lot of business still to take care of. This isn't the finale by any means."

Third-place match: Viera def. Space Coast 3-2 (25-17, 14-25, 25-17, 22-25, 15-6)

Viera captured third place in a five-set win over Space Coast. Both teams traded every set with the Hawks prevailing 15-6 in the final set.

Viera improved to 12-5 and it'll head to the Kentucky Challenge on Sept. 25-26. Space Coast entered its Sept. 24 match versus Bayside with a 9-9 record.

Fifth-place match: Astronaut def. Melbourne 3-2 (19-25, 25-19, 26-24, 20-25, 15-11)

The War Eagles outperformed their seed by two spots to earn fifth place with a pair of road wins. They won their seventh match in the last eight to improve to 10-8. Astronaut's next match is versus Bayside on Sept. 29.

Melbourne sees its 10-match winning streak snapped as it lost its first match since Aug. 22. The Bulldogs drop to 14-4 and it'll host Satellite on Sept. 29.

Seventh-place match: Titusville def. Eau Gallie 3-0 (25-18, 25-16, 25-22)

Titusville entered the conference tournament as the No. 8 seed and it'll finish in seventh following its second sweep of Eau Gallie in six days.

Terriers junior Ja'Dore Pratt finished with a team-high 11 kills and 5 blocks. Senior Hayden Thibert finished with 8 kills and 9 digs. Senior Elise Tueche posted 9 digs and 3 aces.

Titusville improved to 6-5 and it'll play at Merritt Island on Sept. 28. Eau Gallie enters its Sept. 24 match at Brevard HEAT with a 6-7 record.

Ninth-place match: Edgewood def. Rockledge 3-0 (25-23, 25-23, 25-19)

After entering the conference tournament on a five-match losing streak, Edgewood wins back-to-back matches to place ninth.

Red Wolves senior Macy Ferguson spiked 13 kills and dug 8 balls. Sophomore Maya Ferguson and junior Kelsey Kennedy recorded 9 and 8 kills, respectively. Junior Adison Carter tallied 18 assists.

Edgewood moved to 6-7 entering its Sept. 24 match versus Merritt Island Christian. Rockledge dropped to 4-13 before its fourth match in four days on Sept. 24 against Holy Trinity.

13th-place match: Cocoa Beach def. Palm Bay 3-0 (25-12, 25-19, 25-22)

Cocoa Beach finishes one spot higher than its seed following a sweep of the Pirates. The Minutemen improved to 5-9 and it'll head to the two-day Buffalo Stampede at The Villages Charter on Sept. 25-26. Palm Bay dropped to 6-7 and it'll head to Brevard Christian on Sept. 29.

15th-place match: Bayside def. Cocoa 3-0 (25-13, 25-6, 25-11)

Bayside swept Cocoa for the second time this season. The Bears entered their Sept. 24 match at Space Coast with a 5-8 record. They'll play at Odyssey Charter on Sept. 25 to close out the week.

Cocoa fell to 0-8 and it'll host Heritage on Sept. 30.
